"All bound by hands and feet,
And at the open door a prisoner;
And I am called by my right name
Obedience, and so reclaimed.
My cords and also my bonds,
These are various commandments
Which bind the own will
So that it can do nothing according to its liking."
### <term>Discipline</term>
"And I," said she with the file,
"Am called Discipline,
Who everywhere here keeps the order
So that one does not bite into evil.
The file which is in my mouth
Is the rebuke of evil;
I polish and scour everything
Where there is rust and filth.
There is nothing that I do not file away,
Entirely down to the root.
And so that I do everything perfectly
And do not fail in anything,
With this shield of Prudence,
Which is very necessary for this,
I am armed, as you see well;
Thus my bearing is more beautiful.
For certainly if I did not have it,
I would not be sufficient
To correct or to file,
Or to remove the rust of another."

<note>A woodcut illustration depicts several figures seated at a long table in a refectory. They are being served by figures that represent the "dead" or ancestors who have provided for the monastery through their legacies.</note>

"What will be/and the condition
Of these tables/and those eating,
And of these dead whom I see serving,
For which I am greatly astonished."

<column-break/>

<margin>You shall be refreshed before the Lord your God. Deuteronomy 12.</margin>

### <term>Abstinence</term>
"Certainly," she said, "I tell you
That I am the Refectorer
Of all here, and the stewardess,
Who gives to drink and to eat
To everyone as there is need
To sustain the human body
And maintain it in health.
I am named Abstinence,
And armed with the <term>gorgerette</term> <gloss>neck-armor</gloss>
Which is called Sobriety,
By which the taste is guarded;
Also the throat from swallowing
Any morsel that could be harmful.
And do not be astonished
By the dead who feed the living
And serve them devotedly;
Know that these are good people
Who passed away long ago,
Who have given so much of their goods
To the living/that they are sustained
Very sufficiently and fed.
He would certainly be too foolish
Who would not know that service
He had from the dead/who would eat
Their own/and would live from their goods."

<margin>Abstinence truly is to abstain from sins. Distinction 5.</margin>
<margin>Nature is content with few and minimal things. Boethius, book 2 of the Consolation of Philosophy.</margin>
<margin>It is a virtue to have abstained from pleasing goods. Ovid.</margin>

<margin>Rebuke is just when: first it is done in oneself, and afterward it is excited in another. Case 3, question 7.</margin>

### The Pilgrim
<note>A decorative initial V is printed here.</note>
"I saw another pass soon
Toward the refectory going,
Who had a neck-armor
Which closed her throat well.
After her soon I went
And therein I looked.
Several dead people all shrouded,
Giving food to those seated,
And they served them very sweetly,
On their knees and devotedly.
And I saw that the Refectorer
Was she who had the neck-piece,
For she visited all the eaters
And filled their needs.
I wished to know what it was;
To this one I went straight away,
The Refectorer I saw,
Whom I had already followed.
'Tell me,' I said, 'what is your name?'"

<margin>Quare impedit.</margin>
Une deale porta son breve de quare impedit vers Johan de D. et count que un tiel de qui a une
avoweson de la moite de la eglise de B. de queux il presenta un son clerc Thomas de S. que a son
presentement fuit receu et admis et institut de l'evesque en temps de pees en temps le Roy que ore est et
puis la eglise se voida par la mort de dit Thomas par que il appertient a luy a presenter et Johan
luy disturbe a tort. Johan dit que ne poet de dire la voidance ne le presentement de Thomas mes dit que
devant le presentement de dit Thomas un tiel fuit seisi de la moite de la eglise et de la moite de un
manoir de B. a que l'avoweson est appendant et presenta un son clerc Johan de C. que a son
presentement fuit receu et admis et institut de l'evesque en temps de pees en temps le Roy Edward
besael le Roy que ore est et puis de mesme le manoir et de l'avoweson enfeoffa un tiel de qui la
deale ad son estat et puis Johan de C. morust par que le dit feoffor presenta Thomas de S. que
fuit receu et admis et institut de l'evesque en temps le Roy que ore est et puis Thomas de S.
fuit cree en evesque de Hereford par que la eglise se voida par que le Roy seisi les temporalites de l'evesque
de Hereford et puis la mort l'evesque Johan de D. ad suer hors de la main le Roy et
pria aide de luy et de l'evesque de Hereford et le Roy par ses lettres appertient a luy a presenter
par la voidance de dit Thomas par cause de sa creation en evesque de Hereford par que le Roy
presenta un son clerc Johan de B. que fuit receu et admis et institut de l'evesque en temps le Roy
que ore est et puis Johan de B. morust par que le Roy presenta cestui Johan de D. que fuit
receu et admis et institut de l'evesque en temps le Roy que ore est et issint est il persone enpersonne
et n'entendons pas que le Roy voille a cest breve respondre sanz le Roy.

Une femme porta breve de dower vers un tiel et demanda la tierce partie de un mies et de
un carue de terre en B. de la dotation un tiel son baron. Le tenant dit que le baron la femme
ne fuit unques seisi de tiel estat que dower la poet aver et de ceo il se mist en pays et la
femme auxi. Et trove fuit par verdit de pays que le baron la femme fuit seisi de dit mies
et de la terre en son demesne comme de fee et de droit et enfeoffa le tenant et reprist estat a luy
et a sa femme et a les heirs de lour deux corps engendres et puis le baron morust sanz issue
entre eux par que la femme tient la moite de dit mies et de la terre par la forme de la taille
et le tenant l'autre moite par le feoffement le baron et issint le baron ne fuit unques seisi
de tiel estat que dower la poet aver.

<-*Dell'origine della Virtù.*->

**XL.** La virtù tiene la proprietà d'essere d'origine divina (1); conciossiachè queste tre sue parti tutte insieme costituiscono la vera virtù; e ciascuna di esse si trova sempre colle altre due congiunta. E in effetti nella prudenza avvi ancora la fortezza, in quantochè la mente nel ricercare il vero vi si travaglia e dura fatica, nè si ristà sino a che nol ritrovi; vi è anche la temperanza, essendo che è pur cosa savia l'ignorare talune cose. Nella temperanza poi si ritrova la prudenza, che ci consiglia a non trasandare le cose utili alla vita, per non riportarne detrimento; e perciò la Medicina è di origine divina, perchè dettata da questo vero eterno: vi è anche la fortezza, acciocchè sappia egli tenersi lungi dai piaceri. Infine nella fortezza si trova pure la prudenza per difendere l'onesto; vi è poi la temperanza, acciocchè i vincitori non vogliano distruggere i vinti, che possono senza danno serbare in vita.

<-*Della virtù vera.*->

**XLI.** Non avvi adunque virtù alcuna che stia sola, chè ove trovi veramente la virtù, sii certo che vi si trovano tutte le altre insieme riunite: poichè le virtù, che stiano isolate, meritano appena, secondo le parole di S. Agostino, il nome di virtù (2).

<-*Della Grazia divina.*->

**XLII.** Quella virtù poi, che sola dee dirsi vera, e come tale va innanzi a

(1) Cap. III.
(2) Epist. CLXVI; altrimenti XXIX ad Hieronymum, c. 3, n. 11, cap. 4, n. 14.

---

<-*Virtutis divinae origo.*->

**XL.** Virtus divinae originis proprietatem obtinet (1); namque hae tres ejus partes una sunt vera virtus; et quaeque earum semper est cum aliis duabus complicata. Etenim in prudentia et fortitudo inest, ut in vero vestigando laboret, nec in eo nisi explorato acquiescat; inest et temperantia, qua quaedam ignorare sapientia est. In temperantia et prudentia inest, ne quis ad exitium usque sui utilibus vitae rebus abstineat: quare Medicinae origo divina; nam ab hoc vero aeterno dictata: inest et fortitudo, ut sustineat a voluptatibus temperare. In fortitudine et prudentia inest, ut pro honesto pugnet; inest et temperantia, qua victores nolint perdere, quos possunt servare victus.

<-*Virtus vera.*->

**XLI.** Igitur nulla virtus solitaria, et ubi ex vero una ibi omnes Comites adsunt: solae enim virtutes vix est, ut cum Divo Augustino (2) loquar, ut nomen virtutum mereantur.

<-*Divina gratia.*->

**XLII.** Virtus autem, quae una vera, et quia vera, omnes virtutes praestat, non

(1) De qua Cap. III.
(2) Epistola CLXVII; alias XXIX, ad Hieronymum, cap. 3, n. 11, et cap. 4, n. 14, T. II in Edit. Paris.

...oratory, and the art of poetry, then it must properly be called Wisdom. This force of truth, with which the passions are restrained, constitutes *Ethical Virtue*, or the virtue of action, which is called *Moral*.

### Of the Virtue of the Stoics; and of Christian Virtue.

XXXVIII. This force of the truth, which restrains the passions but which is not enough to temper the ferocity from which they spring, is *imperfect moral virtue*, such as St. Augustine considers to be that of the Heathens <note>original: "Ethnicorum"</note> (1). The force of the truth, which fights against cupidity and against the *self-love* <note>original: "amor di sè"</note> that gives birth to it, is *Christian Ethical Virtue*, by means of which man transforms that which most allures the soul into contempt and abjection of himself, and this is called *Humility*, the base and principle of all Christian virtues.

### Three parts of Virtue.

XXXIX. When the mind is moved by virtue to labor in the search for truth, and will not rest until it is attained, it is called *Prudence*: if the soul, by means of virtue, knows how to keep itself far from the unbridled nature of the senses, one then has *Temperance*: if the affections of the soul find themselves sustained by virtue and free from fear, one will have *Fortitude*.

### Della Virtù degli Stoici; e della Virtù Cristiana.

XXXVIII. Questa forza del vero, che raffrena gli affetti , ma che però non basta a temperare la ferocia , da cui essi pullulano , è la *Virtù morale imperfetta*, come S. Agostino vuole che sia quella degli Etnici (1). La forza del vero, che pugna contro la cupidità , e contro l’ *amor di sè* che la partorisce, è la *Virtù Etica Cristiana*, mercè la quale l’uomo trasmuta ciò che più alletta l’animo in dispregio ed abbiezione di sè stesso, ed è detto *Umiltà*, base e principio di tutte le virtù Cristiane.

### Tre parti della Virtù.

XXXIX. Allorchè la mente vien mossa dalla virtù a travagliarsi intorno alla ricerca del vero, nè rimanersi se non poscia conseguito, dicesi *Prudenza*: se l’animo mercè la virtù sappia tenersi lungi dalla sfrenatezza de’ sensi , avrassi allora la *Temperanza*: se gli affetti dell’animo si trovino sostenuti dalla virtù e scevri di timore, si avrà la *Fortezza*.

E a questo modo si ànno per dimostrati i principii della *Morale Cristiana*.

**Della Giustizia.**

**XLIII.** La forza del vero, ossia l'umana ragione che è virtù in quanto pugna contro la cupidità, prende poi il nome di *Giustizia* allorchè s'indirizza a regolare ed equiparare le utilità, il che costituisce l'unico Principio e l'unico Fine del Dritto universale.

**Del Dritto naturale: e definizione dell'equo buono.**

**XLIV.** Le utilità poi, che muovono l'appetito, sono corporee: la misura o regola comune de'corpi è quella che comunemente dicesi proporzione, che i Matematici molto a proposito pel nostro soggetto dimostrano essere duplice, aritmetica ossia semplice, geometrica ossia composta. La proporzione aritmetica è la seguente: *come dieci sta a sei, così sei sta a due*; perchè il sei è maggiore del due per quanto è minore del dieci, cioè dello stesso numero quattro. La proporzione geometrica è questa: *come uno sta a tre, così quattro a dodici*, perchè in ciascuna di queste proporzioni il numero minore è la terza parte di ciascuna quantità. Ora ciò che è eguale allorchè misuri, sarà giusto quando eleggi; essendo che uno è il modo d'assentire sì nell'or-

hominis: sed Dei virtus est, Divina gratia, quae suo lumine Christianis perspicue recta vitae agenda demonstrat; et efficit ut uno genere assensionis invictae et rebus contemplandis et rebus in vita agendis assentiamur (1).
Atque habes *Moralis Christianae Principia* demonstrata.

**De Iustitia.**

**XLIII.** Quae vis veri, seu ratio humana virtus est quantum cum cupiditate pugnat, eadem ipsa est Iustitia quantum utilitates dirigit et exaequat, quae est unum universi Iuris Principium unusque Finis.

**Ius esse in Natura. — Aequum bonum quid?**

**XLIV.** Utilitates autem quae cupiditatem cient, corpore constant: communis corporum mensura seu regula est *commensus* vulgo dicta proportio, quam Mathesis pro nostro argumento demonstrat duplicem, arithmeticam seu simplicem, et geometricam seu comparatam. Arithmetica proportio est, qua ex gr. uti decem se habent ad sex, ita sex se habent ad duo; quia per eumdem numerum quatuor sex excedit duo, et a decem exceditur. Proportio geometrica est, qua uti ex gr. unum se habet ad tria, ita quatuor ad duodecim; quia utrobique minor numerus est triens cujusque assis. ### CANTO. XXI. DELLA SECONDA CANTICA DI DANTHE.

Nobile materia: & nobilmente tracta in questo. XXI canto. Nel quale pone: chome segue do lor cammino furono rigiunti d'una anima: dallaquale intesono la cagione dello scuotere del monte: et del canto dell'anime. Et finalmente conobbon costui essere stato poeta: ne sa za somma uolupta riconobbe lui Virgilio.

LA SETE NATVRAL. Dimostramme potersi di sopra essere innata sete et cupidita nell'huomo di sapere. Et perche la cognitione delle chose diuine e/ quella: per laquale siamo beati. ne questa perfectamente possiamo hauere per nostra industria: ne p uia naturale: se non siamo illuminati dallo spirito sancto: Ilche dinoto Christo nel uangelio di Sa cto Ioanni. IIII. Ca. quando domandando bere al la samaritana al pozzo di Iacob: et ella dinegandogliene: allegando: che e giudei non usano co sa maritari. esso soggiunse: se tu sapessi: chi e quello che t'adimanda bere: tu ne dimanderefti a lui: et esso tidarebbe bere d'una aqua d'una fonte: che fagle in uita etherna. Lagio uinetta adunque do po molte parole l'adomando. et Christo lariépie di spirito sancto. Il perche sapientissimamente al presente dimostra el poeta: che la sete naturale. i. la naturale cupidita del sapere: et conoscere non si satia mai: se non con l'acqua. Onde la giouineta Samaritana adomando la gratia. i. la gratia dello spirito sancto. MITRAVAGLIAVA. e/ tras latione dalle biade gia battute: lequali accioche restino purgate et monde si trauagliano. i. si sanno passare di uaglio in uaglio: chosi l'animo nostro uolendo ritrouare el uero si ua purgando di tem po in tempo. ET PVNGEAMI LA FRETTA dimostra: che aun medesimo tempo l'animo era cupido diuestigar la cagione dello scuotere del monte et del canto dell'anime. Et el corpo hauea accellerarsi nel seguitare suo uiaggio. Ma Statio sopraggiungē do dichiara quello. che ne Danthe. i. la sensualita: ne Virgilio. i. l'intellecto humano: benche illumi nato di molta doctrina: per se potea intendere. Ma statio: elquale per essere affueto a tali chose: le dichia ra. Et pone Statio per l'intellecto humano: elquale si estende a comprendere quello: che per uia di ra gione non si puo comprendere. Et per comparatione dimostra secondo che scriue Luca al. xxiii. cap.

# CANTO XX

...as much as was permitted to my power.
When I felt the mountain tremble
like a thing that falls: whence a chill seized me
such as seizes him who goes to his death.
Surely Delos <note>The Greek island where Apollo and Diana were born; mythologically, it was a floating island until fixed in place.</note> was not shaken so strongly
before Latona made her nest in it
to give birth to the two eyes of heaven <note>The sun (Apollo) and the moon (Diana).</note>.
Then a cry began from every side,
such that the Master turned toward me
saying: "Do not doubt while I lead you."
"Glory to God in the highest" <note>original: "Gloria in excelsis deo"</note> they all
were saying, from what I understood nearby,
from where the cry could be heard.

Where the sun turned as its homeland: so that it moved no more. And he bound it with Gyaros and Mykonos, neighboring islands. The truth they wish it to be is that this island was often shaken by earthquakes. Wherefore the inhabitants went to the oracle of Apollo to ask for a remedy. And he commanded that certain sacrifices be made: and for the future, the dead should not be buried there. Therefore Apollo made it immobile: and that he bound it to Gyaros and Mykonos signifies that the men of those islands inhabited it. It was called first Asteria: afterwards Delos. Which in Greek signifies "clear" and "manifest": because returning to the surface it became manifest: or rather because Apollo gave manifest answers there. **SUCH THAT THE MASTER** turned toward me. **THEN BEGAN** from all sides a cry: Dante felt the mountain shake: and after such shaking he heard that all the spirits of that place with one voice sang: "Glory to God in the highest" <note>original: "Gloria in excelsis deo"</note>: which song the Church uses when with joy and gladness we return thanks to God. This hymn was sung by the angels at the birth of the Savior.

We remained immobile and in suspense
like the shepherds who first heard that song
until the trembling ceased and it was finished.
Then we resumed our holy path,
watching the shadows that lay upon the ground,
returned already to their accustomed weeping.
No ignorance ever with such great war
made me desirous of knowing,
if my memory does not err in this,
as it seemed to me then, thinking upon it;
nor because of the haste was I daring to ask,
nor could I see anything by myself.
Thus I went on, timid and pensive.

...to understand. **THERE.** i.e., in that place. It is easy for anyone in whom there is at least mediocre talent to notice how much this place requires that many and various things be said in detestation of avarice. Because if we could free human minds from such a pernicious disease, the life of mortals would be too happy: and all domestic and civil dissension would cease, as would every foreign war. Nor would we take up many laborious cares, all useless to us, which strip us of honor and peace, and deprive us of that leisure <note>term: "ocio" - referring here to the classical ideal of productive, contemplative rest.</note> which we could spend on things pertaining to our salvation. But if we collect what has been said in various places of this volume, perhaps the listener will feel partly satisfied.

<column-break/>

...they strove to overcome, i.e., to conquer the road, i.e., to pass it. When Dante felt such trembling in the mountain as usually happens with a thing that is about to fall, which first trembles and then drops. And he uses this comparison: that Delos did not shake so strongly when it was moved by earthquakes, before Latona—mother of Apollo and Diana, i.e., of the sun and the moon—gave birth there to the two eyes of heaven. Because the moon and the sun are like two eyes of heaven. Delos is one of the Cyclades islands, of which there is such a fable: Jove loved Asteria; she fled him, and obtained from the gods to be transformed into a quail. But Jove, wanting her to cross the sea, changed her into stone: whence she fell into the water and went to the bottom, where she stayed for a long time. Afterwards Jove, at the prayers of Latona his sister <note>In classical mythology, Latona (Leto) was a lover of Jupiter, not his sister.</note>, who conceived Phoebus and Diana by him, brought her back to the surface and made her an island, but a mobile one. In this island Latona gave birth to the sun and the moon.

<image-desc>A decorative blue drop-cap 'N' featuring white scrollwork and floral motifs.</image-desc> **We remained immobile:** we stayed without going any further. **AND IN SUSPENSE:** doubtful in mind. **LIKE THE SHEPHERDS** who first heard: thus we were stupefied; as were the shepherds to whom the angels, singing this canticle, announced that Christ was born. Whence they, descending from the mountains, heard him in the manger between the ox and the ass. **UNTIL THE TREMBLING CEASED:** until the shaking of the mountain stopped. **AND THAT finished:** and until that whole song was completed. Then we resumed our way, and the souls returned to their accustomed weeping. **NO IGNORANCE** ever [put] so much war: because naturally every man desires to know; it happens that ignorance of a thing, i.e., not knowing it, makes war on man: because it goads him and fights him to seek to know it. I did not dare ask Virgil, nor by myself could I...

<summary>This page depicts a sudden, terrifying earthquake on the mountain of Purgatory followed by the souls singing the "Gloria," which Dante compares to the shepherds at the Nativity. Landino’s commentary explains the earthquake through the Greek myth of Delos and provides a moral reflection on how greed destroys social peace.</summary>

# LOPO SOARES d'ALBEGERIA.

<margin>1516.</margin>
A certain man, who made some signs to the ships, was ordered by Lopo to be approached by Bastiaan Rodrigues with a boat to see what this person desired. He was a renegade who spoke very good Spanish, and he brought a 
<margin>Challenge letter from Suleiman to Lopo Soares.</margin>
Challenge Letter from Suleiman to Lopo Soares, which was full of the usual Turkish boasting and broad claims, challenging him to a battle at sea or on land, one against one, or many against many, to prevent the shedding of the blood of entire armies. And notwithstanding that Gaspar da Silva and Don Alfonso de Menezes begged Lopo Soares very heartily to grant them that honor, he said to the Moor that he should go and tell Suleiman: 
<margin>Answer thereto.</margin>
That he hoped to bring the answer to him on land himself. The next day, as if in satisfaction of their request, Lopo Soares ordered Don Alfonso de Menezes and Denis Fernandes de Mello to go and sound the bottom of the entire channel with a galley; and while they were busy with that, other captains 
<margin>Arson in the Moorish ships.</margin>
went with some boats to set fire to some ships that were lying in the middle of the channel. This being done, he also made himself master of a galleon and immediately set it in a full flame, so that those in the city thought that the fire would spread to them, whereby they began to make every preparation 
<margin>Fear of the inhabitants.</margin>
to flee from there. Seeing all this turmoil, Suleiman began to say: Gentlemen and 
<margin>Suleiman's address to the people.</margin>
Friends, where do you wish to go? What are you afraid of? Do you not see that these people have been here for three days already and have burned nothing but this galleon, which they found defenseless? If you think that they will come to land, you are deceived, for if anyone wants to go to land, he will not burn a galleon, but rather head straight for it and take it; therefore, return to your houses, for this is not the people who would want to risk themselves in such danger.

# Treatise on Armament Technology, Volume 139
## Divination of the Sun (Part II)

### Page 8

The **Jasper Ring** <term>original: *Qiong* (璚); a sash-like atmospheric arc or ring-like phenomenon</term> is shaped like a sash. If **Jasper Rings** appear on all four sides of the sun, or if five colors shimmer and sparkle beside the sun on a single day, this is defined as a **Jasper Ring**.

This omen signifies that the state will have joyful celebrations, yet the wilderness will suffer from wind and rain. When two armies face one another, the side where this phenomenon is positioned will suffer defeat. On a single day, it may also signify the presence of a rebel, or that a minister is plotting treason, leading to the deaths of ten thousand people beneath him. If four or five **Jasper Rings** appear, the number of rebels will correspond to the number of rings observed.

When blue and red vapors are long and stand vertically beside the sun, this is called a **Straight Pillar** <term>original: *Zhi* (直); likely referring to parhelia or sun pillars</term>. Alternatively, if mixed vapors resemble the character for "river" <note>original: *chuan* (川); a character composed of three vertical lines</note> leaning against the sun, this is also a **Straight Pillar**. This portends military chaos and the fragmentation of the national territory.

If there is one **Straight Pillar** beside the sun, it indicates an enemy on that side who desires to declare independence. If there are **Straight Pillars** on all four sides, it indicates that in all four directions there are those who wish to declare themselves independent rulers. The side that launches an attack from the direction where the pillar is located will be victorious.

If there are three **Straight Pillars** and three **Embraces** <term>original: *Bao* (抱); tangent arcs that curve toward the sun, usually seen as a protective or favorable sign</term> beside the sun, those who wish to declare independence will not succeed. The side that follows the direction of the **Embrace** will be victorious and will kill the enemy general.

<summary>This page explains the divinatory meaning of "Jasper Rings" and "Straight Pillars," interpreting these solar phenomena as omens of ministerial treason, territorial fragmentation, and the outcome of regional attempts at independence.</summary>

Along the edges, a 10 <term>li</term> strip is used to manage the <term>hui</term>. Four <term>dian</term> <gloss>administrative units of 400 wells</gloss> make a <term>xian</term> <gloss>district</gloss>. Four [such units] ascend to a <term>tong</term>. The Kings will spread out into Understanding <term>Binah</term> and there will be different fruits from the servant Jacob and Rachel so that they may take the crown in number. 

The numerical value of Kingship <term>Malchut</term> itself is 40 and 70. Know that the "Small Face" <term>Zeir Anpin</term> <gloss>the six Sefirot from Chesed to Yesod</gloss> is known as "two crowns." One is from without, which is before the <term>Chesed</term> <gloss>Loving-kindness</gloss> of the mother, and one is from the hidden Understanding <term>Binah</term>. It was entirely for itself, and the Blessed One gave a portion of His glory to the female forever. These crowns are the two aspects written. 

Do not let it enter your mind that there is any death in the place of judgments. The "Small Face" is the master of the aspects and the worker of the sweetening. For he prepares the daughters as heirs and arranges the waters in the heart of the heart to provide for the daughter, to include her in mercies. In the secret of the worker of the "tithe of the wise," he removes the accusations from her. 

Know that there is no pair of <term>Tiferet</term> and <term>Malchut</term> except when they are aroused. There are eighty branches. <term>Chesed</term> is the branch for the future, like the aspect of reaching the prayer shawl. This occurs day by day. And so in the nature of everything, it is covered in the morning. This happens four times, specifically in the portion of <term>Bereshit</term> <gloss>Genesis</gloss>, according to the reason of the creation of man. Outside of this, they are "two countenances" back-to-back, and at the time it is written that "the Lord did not save," it means the "Small Face" included right and left over the earth. 

He reigned in his place and they dreamed of passing through it. He passed through them to preserve the bodies. Man should not cling to it except in the aspect of "face to face." Therefore, there is no foundation <term>Yesod</term> below in this world, nor above in <term>Tiferet</term> and <term>Malchut</term>. They do not need to ascend to be in the palace of Understanding <term>Binah</term>. 

The branches from <term>Tiferet</term> and <term>Malchut</term> are the six edges. Thus, a man and his wife among the lower ones are a hint to the letters <term>Vav</term> and <term>He</term>. <margin>The ranks of perfection in prophecy consist of revealing Truths. Sainthood is dominant in the emergence of [the Prophet].</margin>
The spirits of the <term>Paraclete</term> <gloss>Faraqlit</gloss>. It is attributed to the <term>Paraclete</term>, spelled with a 'f', then an 'a', then a 'r' with a <term>kasra</term>, then a silent 'q', then a 'l' with a <term>kasra</term>, then a 'y', then a 't', and an 'a'. It is a Hebrew word <note>likely Syriac/Greek in origin</note> meaning "the Divider between Truth and Falsehood." 
It refers to the manifestation of Sainthood <note>original: "wilaya"</note>, which is the inner aspect of Prophecy. As the Messiah, Jesus son of Mary, foretold — and the explanation of the name's meaning will follow — when he said: "I am going to my Father and your Father," meaning "my Lord and your Lord." We previously mentioned that the ancients used to call the Principles "Fathers," but not in the sense understood by the Christians. This is indicated by his saying "and your Father." 
"He will send you the <term>Paraclete</term> who will distinguish between you by the Truth." It is said that his intention was our Master, the Seal of Prophets, peace and blessings be upon him. His emergence was upon Prophecy. Therefore, you see the forms of his legal symbols are extremely delicate. The signs of his comprehensive speech and superior symbols of Truth are extremely clear. This is as he indicated by his saying, peace and blessings be upon him: "I have come to you with the easy-going, tolerant, white way." 
"Ease" and "tolerance" refer to the delicacy and subtlety. "White" refers to the appearance of Truths from beneath the fine veils. Since his emergence was the most intimate of the ranks of Prophecy in terms of delicacy, subtlety, and the dominance of Sainthood, Prophecy was sealed with his holy emergence. Nothing remained after him except pure Sainthood. 
My father, the Messiah, said: "The <term>Paraclete</term> whom my Father sends in my name will teach you all things." This means the interpretation of every form of the symbols I have brought to you in word and deed. His saying "in my name" means he is called "the Messiah" <note>The Anointed</note> because he anoints with light. 
"He shall judge" — meaning he shall overflow with the shining Light, which is the elixir of knowledge and power, as previously mentioned. This was indicated in the Quran where it is said: "Then surely upon Us is its explanation." The word "then" implies a delay. He means it is known from the saying "Then surely upon Us is its explanation" that the complete revealing of the truths of what was foretold by the symbols of the revealed laws

الفائقة بالحقائق في غاية الظهور كما اشار بقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم اتيتكم
بالسهلة السمحة البيضاء فالسهولة والسماحة اشارة الى الرقة واللطافة
والبيضاء الى ظهور الحقائق من تحت نكد الحجب الرقايق وحيث كان نشأته
انس ما يكون للنبوة من مراتب الرقة واللطافة وغلبة الولاية ختم النبوة
بنشأته المقدسة وما بقى بعده الا الولاية الصرفة وقال ابي المسيح ان الفار
قليطا الذي يرسله ابي باسمي ويعلمكم كل شيء اي تاويل كل صورة من الاوضاع
التي اتيتكم بها قولا وفعلا وقوله باسمي اي يسمى بالمسيح لانه يمسح بالنور
يقضي اي يفيض بالنور الشارق الذي هو اكسير العلم والقدرة كما سبق وقد
اليه اشير في المصحف حيث قيل ثم ان علينا بيانه وثم للتراخي يعني ان يعلم من قوله
ثم ان علينا بيانه ان تمام الكشف عن حقايق ما انبا به صور الاوضاع المنزلة

And if it is large, its edges do not meet because it is circular, spaced apart, and of varying shape, and a lot of meat has been lost from it, so its treatment is suturing and preventing the accumulation of moisture in it by using astringent diluents, and using the plasters that we will mention. If it is deep, then scarring may also stick it together [through] frequent pulling toward the covering. Sometimes the covering gathers... that is where pulling it with a bandage to secure it does not help, as we will show, especially where the firm pulling does not fall on the base of the depth, so materials flow into it because of its weakness. The placement is necessary, and its circumstances are mentioned in the chapter on ulcers. If pulling is needed from its place, place cotton or what serves its function on its face to dry it, especially where the pulling does not fall on the base, [as this is] sufficient for it. And its pouring... its pouring, it is not possible for the bad material to pour off it, or it contains bone or a fracture... and a very bad moisture has arisen from it, and it is then in the category of ulcers rather than abscesses. The scholar said: When the wound needs a bandage that brings the lips together if adhesion and healing are desired. But if it needs meat to grow in it, it does not need that, but it needs, at one time, a bandage that strikes the place, and at another time, a bandage for [the area] behind it, so it does not hold the medicine on it. He said: It is necessary that the position of the wound be a place from which the [superfluity] pours out always by its nature, either by placing the abdomen there, or by shaping it in that shape. <term>Khorasan</term> and reformed it until it was stable. <term>Raja' ibn Abi al-Dahhak</term>, who was the husband of <term>al-Fadl ibn Sahl</term>'s sister, governed all of <term>Khorasan</term>. <term>al-Ma'mun</term> arrived in <term>Baghdad</term> in the middle of <term>Safar</term> in the year two hundred and four. <term>Khorasan</term> had completely deteriorated under <term>Raja' ibn Abi al-Dahhak</term>, so <term>al-Ma'mun</term> appointed <term>Ghassan ibn Abbad</term> over <term>Khorasan</term>. He reformed it and it became stable under his hand. <term>al-Ma'mun</term> supported him, and he stayed for the remainder of the year two hundred and four and several months of the year two hundred and five. Then <term>Talhah ibn Tahir</term> died in the year two hundred and fifteen. <term>al-Ma'mun</term> had previously appointed <term>Abd Allah ibn Tahir</term> over the provinces of <term>al-Jabal</term> and <term>Azerbaijan</term>. The red pavilion enters the forest as the white rain rises. The wind comes to the rush pond before the auspicious autumn. When the frost arrives, the tiny evening does not open.

### Waking Early at Cheongho

The water is bright, and I know the energy of the Way is before the mountain. I see the spirit clearly and could paint the new clearing. The color is deep blue as the sun rises in the east.

### Evening View at Cheongho

A new coolness is born after the rain. I wake from sleep and go up before the tower. The fields are moist, and the cicadas sing in the trees. The river is flat, and seagulls pass through the sky.

### Blocked by Rain at the Small Leisure House

The dark forest mist is like water. In the house by the stream, the wine is like spring. This was formerly a place for seeking flowers. Now I am a person blocked by the rain.

好卦大才，至聖端日威嚴以臣，駐邪立本，一事切序，一亮也。

धात्रीवागीश्वर्यश्च पञ्च । एतास्ताश्च देवीर्गयिका यजेत् । तत्प्रसिद्धं पद्धतिषु ॥१०९॥

ततश्चान्तस्त्रिकोणेऽपि गुरुपङ्क्ति त्रिधा स्थिताम् ।
ततस्तस्य श्रीचक्रस्य अन्तस्त्रिकोणे त्रिधा स्थितां दिव्यसिद्धमानवौघत्रयवतीं गुरुपङ्क्ति शिवादिस्वगुरुपर्यन्तानां गुरूणां पङ्क्तिः परम्परा ताम् । अपिशब्दाद् यजेदित्यनुषङ्गः । गुरुपरम्परा गुरुमुखादेव ज्ञातव्या, न लोकतः । न च पुस्तके लिखिता, अत्यन्तरहस्यत्वात् ॥

तदन्तश्च महादेवीं तामावाह्य यजेत् पुनः ॥११०॥
महापद्मवनान्तस्थां कारणानन्दविग्रहाम् ।
मदङ्कोपाश्रयां देवीमिच्छाकामफलप्रदाम् ॥१११॥
भवतीं

तदन्तः श्रीचक्रस्य मध्ये बैन्दवाख्ये चक्रे । तां महापद्मवनान्तस्थां 'महापद्मवनान्तस्थे वाग्भवे गुरुपादुकाम्' (३१५) इत्यत्रोपादितरूपाम् । अकुला-

त्रिपुरसुन्दरी की गायिकाओं के रूप में पूजा करे। यह सारा विषय पद्धति-ग्रन्थों में प्रसिद्ध है ॥१०९॥

तब श्रीचक्र के मध्यत्रिकोण में त्रिधा स्थित गुरुपंक्ति की पूजा करे ॥
इसके बाद श्रीचक्र के अन्दर बीच में विद्यमान त्रिकोण में दिव्य, सिद्ध और मानवौघ के क्रम से तीन भागों में विभक्त गुरुपंक्ति की, शिव से लेकर अपने गुरु तक चली आई गुरुपरम्परा की भी पूजा करे। त्रिधा विभक्त इस गुरुपरम्परा का ज्ञान अपने गुरु के मुँह से ही प्राप्त करना चाहिये। लौकिक परम्परा से इसका ज्ञान नहीं हो सकता। यह परम्परा अत्यन्त गोपनीय होने से पुस्तक में भी नहीं लिखी जाती ॥

उस त्रिकोण रूपी महापद्मवन में विराजमान, कारणानन्द शरीरवाली इच्छा-अनुसार सभी कामनाओं को पूरा करने वाली, मेरे अंक में विराजमान महादेवी त्रिपुरसुन्दरी का आवाहन कर पूजन करे ॥११०-११२॥

'महापद्मवनान्तस्थ' पद की व्याख्या पहले (३१५) की जा चुकी है। तदनुसार श्रीचक्र के मध्य में स्थित त्रिकोणान्तर्गत बैन्दव चक्र में विद्यमान अकुल नाम का अधोमुख

<header>Chapter III ] With Dipikā Commentary Translation 301</header>

...the group of sixteen modifications, their objects, and the entire expansion of the universe shines as the <term>Śrī Cakra</term>. ||108||

He describes the worship of the <term>Śrī Cakra</term> beginning with "Gaṇeśa" and ending with "having performed the circle worship" (3.168)—

"One should worship Gaṇeśa and Dūtarī, as well as Kṣetreśa and Dūtikā,
At the external gate, O Goddess, and also the goddesses such as Svastikā." ||109||

One should worship Gaṇeśa at the doorframe of the <term>Śrī Cakra</term>, his power Dūtarī, Kṣetreśa known as Baṭuka, and his power Dūtikā. It is said in the *Saṅketa-paddhati*:

"He who is capable of dispelling the darkness of the night of great delusion, which is duality and non-duality,
The unique Gaṇeśa, along with Dūtarī, shines like the sun.
Where the supreme expansion of intuition occurs, another like the moon,
Baṭuka, who is full of the dance, shines along with Dūtī."

At the external gate, in the region outside the door of the <term>Śrī Cakra</term>, one should worship the goddesses such as Svastikā—namely, Sarasvatī, Śrī, Durgā, and Bhadrakālī, these four. The term "Svastikā, etc." is a compound <note>meaning Svastikā is the first of these</note>. Svāhā, Śubhaṅkarī, Gaurī, Lokadhātrī, and Vāgīśvarī—these are the five. The practitioner should worship these goddesses. This is famous in the ritual manuals. ||109||

<summary>The text provides specific instructions for the ritual worship of deities at the gates of the Sri Chakra, framing them as aspects of consciousness that clear away dualistic ignorance.</summary>

श्रीचक्रपूजामाह "गणेशम्" इत्यादिना "चक्रपूजां विधाय" (३।१६८) इत्यन्तेन—

श्रीचक्रद्वारशाखयोगणेशं तच्छक्ति दूतरीं क्षेत्रेशं बटुकाख्यं तच्छक्ति दूतिकां च यजेत्। तदुक्तं संकेतपद्धत्याम्—

प्रतिभायाः परोल्लासो निशाकर इवापरः।
दूतीयुक्तः स जयति बटुकस्ताण्डवान्वितः ॥ इति।

इनके विषय, पुर्यष्टक, सोलह विकार पर्यन्त इस समस्त विश्वप्रपंच का स्वरूप धारण कर लेती है और इसी का नाम श्रीचक्र है ॥१०८॥

अब यहाँ १०९ से १६८ पर्यन्त श्लोकों में श्रीचक्र की पूजाविधि बताई जा रही है—
हे देवि! श्रीचक्र के बाह्य द्वार पर गणेश, दूतरी, क्षेत्रेश तथा दूतिका और स्वस्तिका आदि देवियों की पूजा करे ॥१०९॥

श्रीचक्र के द्वार की दोनों तरफ गणेश और उसकी शक्ति दूतरी की तथा क्षेत्रेश (बटुक) और उसकी शक्ति दूतिका की पूजा करे। संकेतपद्धति में बताया गया है—

द्वैत और अद्वैत की महामोह रूपी रात्रि के घने अन्धकार का, अज्ञान का नाश करने में एकमात्र गणेश ही अपनी शक्ति दूतरी के साथ सूर्य के समान समर्थ हैं। उनकी जय हो। प्रतिभा का जहाँ परम उत्कर्ष हुआ है, चन्द्रमा के समान जो आलोक से परिपूर्ण है, ताण्डव नृत्य में रत, अपनी शक्ति दूती के साथ विराजमान बटुकभैरव की जय हो ॥

धोमुखसहस्रदलं कमलं महापद्मवनम्। मदङ्कोपाश्रयाम् अनाश्रितस्य¹ स्वप्रकाशात्मनो ममाऽङ्कस्थाम्। कारणानन्दविग्रहाम्। कारणं नाम² हेतुद्रव्यम्। अत्रैव वक्ष्यति—"क्षेत्राणां पतये मह्यं बलिं कुर्वीत हेतुना" (३।१९९) इति। द्रव्यपानेन तेन य आनन्दः, स एव विग्रह आकारो यस्यास्ताम्। कोऽर्थः? शोधितामृतभूतद्रव्यपानपरिस्फुरत्परमानन्दमात्रशरीरामित्यर्थः। भवतीम् अनाश्रितां [मम³ देवीं विमर्शत्मिकाम्। इच्छाकामफलप्रदाम् इच्छया यत् काम्यते फल४ तस्य सर्वस्य दात्रीम्।

> महापद्मवनान्तस्थे कारणानन्दविग्रहे।
> सर्वभूतहिते मातरेह्येहि परमेश्वरि॥

इति मन्त्रेण आवाह्य यजेत्।
ननु महापद्मवनान्तस्थामित्यनेनैवानाश्रितो देवोऽनाश्रिता देवी चाऽत्र चक्रे समावाह्य कामेश्वरीकामेश्वररूपेण पूज्याविति कथमवसीयत इति चेदुच्यते—महापद्मवनान्तस्थः सकलागमशास्त्राणां वक्ता देवोऽप्यनाश्रित एव, तच्छक्तिरनाश्रिताऽत एव। अन्यथा महापद्मवनान्तस्थां मदङ्कोपाश्रयां भवतीमिति वचनं

सहस्रदल कमल महापद्मवन कहलाता है। यह देवी उसमें विराजमान है। यह देवी अनाश्रित स्वप्रकाशमय शिवस्वरूप की, अर्थात् मेरी, गोद में बैठी हुई है। कारण हेतु-द्रव्य को कहते हैं। यहीं आगे (३।१९९) क्षेत्रपाल को बलि देने के प्रसंग में इस अर्थ में हेतु शब्द का प्रयोग हुआ है। कारण द्रव्य के पान से जो आनन्द उच्छलित होता है, वही उस शक्ति का स्वरूप है। इसका अभिप्राय यह है कि शोधन के कारण अमृतस्वरूप हुए द्रव्य के पान से उच्छलित आनन्द मात्र ही उस देवी का शरीर है। वह देवी दूसरी कोई नहीं है, स्वयं इस शास्त्र का श्रवण करने वाली तुम ही हो। अनाश्रित स्वरूप मेरी विमर्शत्मिका अनाश्रिता शक्ति तुम ही हो। साधक अपनी इच्छानुसार जिस फल की कामना करता है, वह भगवती उसे सब कुछ देती है। इसका 'महापद्म' इत्यादि मन्त्र से आवाहन कर पूजन करे। इस मन्त्र का अर्थ है—

महापद्मवन में स्थित, करणानन्द स्वरूपिणी, सब प्राणियों का कल्याण करने वाली हे परमेश्वरि माता ! आओ आओ ।।

यहाँ प्रश्न उठता है कि 'महापद्मवनान्तस्थाम्' इस पद से अनाश्रित देव और अनाश्रिता देवी का यहाँ आवाहन कर कामेश्वर और कामेश्वरी के रूप में पूजन किया जाता है। इसका निर्णय कैसे होगा? इसका उत्तर यह है कि महापद्मवन में बैठकर समस्त शास्त्रों का उपदेश करने वाले भगवान् अनाश्रित ही हैं। इसीलिये उनकी शक्ति अना-

...twice, facing all directions. These are to be known as the **Gurus** <note>original: "Guru," another name for Jupiter, meaning "Teacher" or "Heavy with knowledge"</note>; thus they are proclaimed.

### Now, the Meditation

Adorned with gems like those of Indra, the Lord of the World, who is the life of all that lives. The Lord of Speech <note>original: "Vākpati"</note>, whose intellect and beauty are vast, who is Prosperity herself. With a crown that holds the entire universe of beings, he whose lotus feet are seen at the limit of vision. With a pure mind and marvelous intent, for the sake of all auspiciousness, may the Lord of Speech be well-pleased with those of unwavering heart. ॥ 1 ॥

There is none equal in pervasiveness; he is the Priest of the Gods. The knower of all deities, the Teacher—salutations, salutations to him. ॥ 3 ॥

The Teacher of the gods, wearing yellow garments, the Lord of the Sages. I bow to him who lives as the most excellent of the moving stars. ॥ 4 ॥

The Teacher of the gods and the seers, shining like gold, the relative of the three worlds, the peaceful one—I bow to Jupiter. ॥ 5 ॥

The proclaimer of all scriptures, the expander of all actions, the giver of all success, the god who is affectionate toward his circle of devotees. ॥ 6 ॥ <margin>6</margin>

The giver of boons, the peaceful one, worshiped by the thirty gods <note>a traditional grouping of the Vedic pantheon</note>, the supreme. For him whose seat is the sacred grass and who is of golden hue, this offering is made. ॥ 7 ॥

Clad in yellow garments, the holy one, endowed with the splendor of the sun.

**Thus ends the Ritual Assignment for the Teacher.**

*Om*, [earth, atmosphere, heavens], salutations to the **thumbs**.
"One [form] of yours is bright, the other is fit for sacrifice..." <note>original: "śukraṃ te anyad yajataṃ te anyad," a verse from Rig Veda 6.58.1 usually associated with the sun or brightness, here used for the ritual installation</note>
"...like the two-fold paths of the sun." To the **middle fingers**, salutations.
"You protect all magic, O self-dependent power." To the **ring fingers**, salutations.
"May your auspicious gift be near to us." To the **ring fingers**, salutations. <note>The text repeats the ring finger assignment, likely a scribal duplication or indicating a specific rhythmic touch</note>
Having uttered the entire mantra, to the **palms and backs of the hands**.

### Now begins the Six-Limbed Ritual Assignment

*Om*, [earth, atmosphere, heavens], salutations to the **heart**.
"One [form] of yours is bright, the other is fit for sacrifice"—*Svāhā* <note>a ritual exclamation used when offering into fire</note> to the **head**.
"The day and night of various forms"—*Vaṣaṭ* <note>a ritual exclamation for empowerment</note> to the **topknot**.
"You protect all magic, O self-dependent power"—*Huṃ* <note>a protective, seed-syllable sound</note> to the **armor** <note>the torso/shoulders</note>.
"May your auspicious gift be near to us"—*Vauṣaṭ* to the **three eyes**.
Having uttered the entire mantra—*Phaṭ* <note>a sharp sound used to dispel obstacles</note> to the **weapon** <note>symbolized by snapping fingers or clapping</note>.

## Leaf 1 (Top)

As <term>Vidya Lakshmi</term> <gloss>the Goddess of Knowledge and Prosperity</gloss> is seen, so also is <term>Saraswati</term> <gloss>the Goddess of Wisdom and Arts</gloss> seen. She is the giver of all knowledge and the provider of all wealth.
<note>original: "Vidyalakshmi yatha drishta tatha drishta Saraswati | Sarva vidya pradatree cha sarva sampath pradayinee ||"</note>

To the most auspicious of all auspicious things, to the one who brings success to all goals, to the protector, the three-eyed one, the golden goddess, to <term>Narayani</term> <gloss>the feminine aspect of the Supreme Lord</gloss>, I bow to you.
<note>original: "Sarva mangala mangalye Shive sarvartha sadhike | Sharanye tryambake Gauri Narayani namostute ||"</note>

May there be success in all knowledge.

## Leaf 2 (Bottom)

O Goddess who dwells in the lotus, the pure one, worshipped by everyone, the beloved of Vishnu, I bow to you. O Queen of the Universe, be pleased with me.
<note>original: "Padme padmalaye devi suchite sarva pujite | Vishnupriye namastubhyam praseeda jagadeeshwari ||"</note>

To the most auspicious of all auspicious things, to the one who brings success to all goals, to the protector, the three-eyed one, the golden goddess, to <term>Narayani</term>, I bow to you.

May there be success in all knowledge.

<note>Two circular holes used for binding the cord are visible in the center of each palm leaf.</note>

खारिज आदि कैसा है इतना निश्चय करके पूछनेवालेके निर्गम
भेद इसका शुभाशुभ परिणाम मुखसे वा परिश्रमसे कहना ॥ १७ ॥
इस प्रकार निर्गमनादि सब प्रश्न विचार के पूछनेवालेके आगे ।
इसमें रम्मालकी चित्तवृत्ति स्थिर रमलशास्त्र एवं गुरुमें विश्र्वास
और चित्तकी शुद्धिहो तब प्रश्नसिद्धि होती है ॥ १८ ॥

->इति निर्गमादिप्रकारः ॥<-

->अथेन्किलावप्रयोजनम् ।<-

इदानीमिन्किलावोत्थात्प्रश्नाच्चापि फलं ब्रुवे ॥

खिलेत्वागमस्येव शुभेस्यातां तुसिद्धिदे ॥ २० ॥
सावितेचशुभेतद्वत्स्थिरकार्यस्यसिद्धिदे ॥ मध्य-
मेसबलेसिद्धि रल्पसिद्धिश्चनिर्बले ॥ २१ ॥ विपर्य-
यनसिद्धिः स्याच्छुभाद्यत्रापि पूर्ववत् ॥ संविचा-
र्यवदेत्सर्वप्रश्नखण्डोपिपूर्ववत् ॥ २२ ॥ मुष्टि-
मूकशरुत्पत्राऽवधिप्रश्नहराभिधाः ॥ इन्किलावं
विनासिद्धास्तस्मादेषु न तद्भवेत् ॥ २३ ॥ एवं
सामान्यतः प्रोक्तः सर्वगेहेषुनिर्णयः ॥ यद्यद्गेहेवि-
शेषं च तत्तद्गेहेऽधुनाब्रुवे ॥ २४ ॥

**टीका-** अब इन्किलावका प्रयोजन कहतेहैं कि इस समय इन्कि-
लावसे उत्पन्न प्रश्नसे कहनेमें यदि १५ वें घरमें जमात होती
उसके मूल १३ । १४ से फल कहना ॥ १९ ॥ सो ऐसा है कि

<meta>This page continues the specific rules for geomantic interpretation within the "Ramala Navaratna." It transitions from questions of movement (Departure and Arrival) to "Fixed" questions—those concerning things intended to stay or remain stable (like building a house or staying in a job). It then provides a technical "tie-breaker" rule for when the figures in a reading contradict one another.</meta>

<page-num>५७</page-num>
<header>The Fifth Gem [5.]</header>

### Now, the Fixed Question.

> -> In a fixed question, when both figures are Auspicious and **Incoming** or **Fixed**, then the task will be firm and successful due to happiness. If they are Inauspicious, success comes only through great effort. ॥ १४ ॥ **Outgoing** and **Mobile** figures act as the destroyers of a fixed task. In this manner, the greatest knower of geomancy should explain all three types of questions. ॥ १५ ॥ <-

**Commentary**—Now the rule for the **Fixed Question** <term>Sthira-prashna</term> <note>questions regarding permanent or long-term situations</note> is explained: In a fixed question, if the geomantic figures are **Fixed** <term>Sabit</term> <note>original: *thābit*; figures representing stability</note> and **Incoming** <term>Dakhil</term> <note>original: *dākhil*; figures representing entry</note>, and they are Auspicious, then the fixed task will be successfully completed. If those same Fixed and Incoming figures are Inauspicious, the task will be achieved only after much hardship. ॥ १४ ॥ **Outgoing** <term>Kharij</term> <note>original: *khārij*; figures representing departure</note> and **Mobile** <term>Munkalib</term> <note>original: *munqalib*; figures representing change or reversal</note> figures are the destroyers of any task intended to be stable or fixed. In this way, a practitioner who is the best among those who know geomancy <term>Rammal</term> should deliver the judgment for the group of questions. ॥ १५ ॥

### Now, the Rule for Resolving Doubts.

> -> When two or three figures do not agree, and their results conflict regarding the task's outcome, then multiply the house of the question by its half. From that resulting figure, speak as before. ॥ १६ ॥ In a question, the wise practitioner should also observe the strength of the generated figure, its elemental nature, and whether it is Outgoing or otherwise. He should then describe the various differences such as the querent's departure, based on whether the indicators are Auspicious or Inauspicious, or lead to happiness or struggle. ॥ १७ ॥ In this way, the practitioner should state everything from the conclusion of the question to the person asking, without any doubt. If one's heart is pure and has faith in the Master of Geomancy, then success is certain. ॥ १८ ॥ <-

**Commentary**—If, while interpreting a question and its result, two different types of figures appear which contradict one another—for example, if one figure indicates stability <term>Sthira</term> and the other indicates movement <term>Chara</term>, or if one is **Outgoing** and another is **Incoming**, or if one is Auspicious and the other is Inauspicious—then one must use a "tie-breaker." Multiply the value of the **Fourteenth House** <note>represented here as the 'Question Segment'</note> and from the resulting figure produced by that multiplication, the practitioner should explain the answer using the previously described methods. ॥ १६ ॥ Within the question, one must also evaluate the inherent strength of the figure that has been produced. Consider its natural disposition <term>Svabhava</term> based on its position, and whether it is **Outgoing** <term>Kharij</term> or of another type. One should then tell the querent whether there will be a departure or other outcomes, and whether it will result in good or bad fortune, or happiness versus hard labor. ॥ १७ ॥ In this manner, the practitioner should confidently explain the entire conclusion of the reading to the querent. If the practitioner’s own mind is pure and they possess a heart that trusts in the **Master of Geomancy** <note>or "Guru of Ramal"</note>, then the prediction will certainly come to fruition. ॥ १८ ॥

<vocab>रमल (Ramal: Geomancy), रम्माल (Rammal: Geomancer), स्थिरप्रश्न (Sthira-prashna: Fixed question), साबित (Sabit: Fixed figure), दाखिल (Dakhil: Incoming figure), खारिज (Kharij: Outgoing figure), मुन्कलीव (Munkaliv: Mobile figure), शकल (Shakal: Geomantic figure/shape), संशयेनियामकम् (Sanshayeniyamakam: Resolver of doubts), सिद्ध (Siddha: Proven/Successful)</vocab>

<summary>This page defines how to interpret "Fixed" questions—where Incoming and Fixed figures signify success—and provides a mathematical method for resolving contradictory figures in a reading. It emphasizes the importance of the practitioner's mental purity and faith for an accurate divination.</summary>
<keywords>Fixed Questions, Sabit, Dakhil, Kharij, Munkalib, resolution of doubt, geomantic math, 14th house, practitioner ethics</keywords>

The Vāyu-purāṇa certainly reckons Kaśyapa, with his father-in-law Daksha and other sages, among the Prajāpatis, but he does not belong to the seven original Prajāpatis of whom his father Marīci is one, nor to the ten enumerated by Manu (i. 35). tāna, ‘the spreading part of a creeper.’ Jaṭā-maṇḍala is the circle or bundle of matted entangled hair which ascetics allowed to grow on the crown of their heads, and which fell in long clotted tresses over the back and shoulders. Jaṭā is, especially, Siva’s hair so plaited and arranged, through which the Ganges meandered before its descent upon the earth. Niṭitam = pūritam, K. Sthāṇuḥ = śākhā-hīnas taru-skandhaḥ. Abhyarkavimbam = sūrya-maṇḍalābhimukham, K. The Mackenzie MS. has adhyarka°.

² ‘Possessed of the Mandāra-tree reared by Aditi.’ This was one of the five trees of Svarga (see p. 272, n. 1), and is probably the tree intended here, as, in verse 176, the Kalpa tree also is said to have graced Kaśyapa’s retreat, which the commentator thence infers to have been located in part of Svarga. Mandāra, ‘the coral tree,’ may also mean ‘swallow-wort.’

³ Amṛta, ‘the beverage of immortality,’ ‘the nectar’ of the Hindū gods, supposed to be a liquid substance distilled by the moon, who is thence called amṛta-sū, ‘nectar-producer;’ amṛtādhāra, ‘nectar-repository.’

यथा रूपस्याऽऽलोकस्तथा रूपज्ञानं, विकारकारणं मनसो विषयान्तरम् । यथाऽग्निः पाक्यस्य । प्रत्ययकारणं धूमज्ञानमग्निज्ञानस्य । प्राप्तिकारणं योगाङ्गानुष्ठानं विवेकख्यातेः ।
वियोगकारणं तदेवाशुद्धेः । अन्यत्वकारणं यथा सुवर्णस्य सुवर्णकारः । एवमेकस्य स्त्रीप्रत्ययस्याविद्या मूढत्वे द्वेषो दुःखत्वे

मिन्द्रियद्वारा वा स्वतो वा विषयस्य संस्क्रियाऽभिव्यक्तिस्तस्याः कारणं यथा रूपस्याऽऽलोकः । विकारकारणं मनसो विषयान्तरम् । यथा हि कण्डोः समाहितमनसो वल्लकीविपञ्च्यमानपञ्चमस्वरश्रवणसमनन्तरमुन्मीलिताक्षस्य <gloss>१</gloss> स्वरूपलावण्ययौवनसंपन्नामप्सरसं प्रम्लोचामीक्षमाणस्य समाधिमपहाय तस्यां सक्तं मनो बभूवेति । अत्रैव निदर्शनमाह—यथाऽग्निः पाक्यस्य <gloss>२</gloss> तण्डुलादेः कठिनायवयवसंनिवेशस्य प्रशिथिलावयवसंयोगलक्षणस्य विकारस्य कारणम् । सत एव विषयस्य प्रत्ययकारणं धूमज्ञानमग्निज्ञानस्येति । ज्ञायत इति ज्ञानमग्निश्चासौ ज्ञानं चेत्यग्निज्ञानं तस्य । एतदुक्तं भवति—वर्तमानस्यैवाग्नेर्ज्ञेयस्य प्रत्ययकारणतया कारणमिति । औत्सर्गिकी निरपेक्षाणां कारणानां कार्यक्रिया प्राप्तिस्तस्याः कुतश्चिदपवादोऽप्राप्तिः । यथा निम्नोपसर्पणस्वभावानामपां प्रतिबन्धः सेतुना तथैहापि बुद्धिसत्त्वस्य सुखप्रकाशशीलस्य स्वाभाविकी सुखविवेकख्यातिजनकता प्राप्तिः । सा कुतश्चिद्धर्मात्तमसो वा प्रतिबन्धान्न भवति । धर्माद्योगाङ्गानुष्ठानाद्वा तदपनये तदप्रतिबद्धवृत्तिस्वभावत एव तज्जनकता तदाप्नोति । यथा वक्ष्यति—निमित्तमप्रयोजकं प्रकृतीनां वरणभेदस्तु ततः क्षेत्रिकवदिति ।

तदेवं विवेकख्यातिलक्षणकार्यापेक्षया प्राप्तिकारणमुक्तम् । अवान्तरकार्यापेक्षया तु तदेव वियोगकारणमित्याह—वियोगकारणमिति । अन्यत्वकारणमाह—अन्यत्वकारणं यथा सुवर्णकारः सुवर्णस्य, कटककुण्डलकेयूरादिभ्यो भिन्नाभिन्नस्य भेदविवक्षया कटकादिभिन्नस्याभेदविवक्षया कटकाद्यभिन्नस्य सुवर्णस्य कुण्डलादन्यत्वम् । तथा च कटककारी सुवर्णकारः कुण्डलादभिन्नसुवर्णादन्यत्कुर्वन्नन्यत्वकारणम् । अग्निरपि पाक्यस्यान्यत्वकारणं यद्यपि तथाऽपि धर्मिणो धर्मयोः पुलाकत्वतण्डुलत्वयोर्भेदाविवक्षया धर्मयोरुपजनापायेऽपि धर्म्यनुवर्तत इति न तस्यान्यत्वं शक्यं वक्तुमिति विकारमात्रकारणत्वमुक्तमिति न संकरः । न च संस्थानभेदो धर्मिणोऽन्यत्वकारणमिति व्याख्येयम् । सुवर्णकार इत्यस्यासंगतेः । बाह्यमन्यत्वकारणमुपन्यस्याऽऽध्यात्मिकमुदाहरति—एवमेकस्येति । अविद्या कमनीयेयं कन्यकेत्यादिज्ञानम् <gloss>४</gloss> । तन्मोहयोगात्त एव स्त्रीप्रत्ययो

<header>Pātañjala Yoga Sūtras</header>
<meta>Sūtra 28</meta>

The eight limbs of Yoga will be described. Through their practice, the five-fold error (<term>viparyaya</term>), which is the form of impurity, is destroyed. Upon its destruction, there is a manifestation of correct knowledge. As the practices are performed, the impurity gradually becomes thin. As it thins, the light of knowledge, corresponding to the sequence of destruction, increases. This increase attains its peak up to discriminative realization, meaning until the knowledge of the nature of the <term>guṇas</term> and the <term>puruṣa</term>. The practice of the limbs of Yoga is the cause of the separation from impurity, just as an axe is the cause of separation from what is to be cut. As for discriminative realization, it is the cause of attainment, just as merit (<term>dharma</term>) is for happiness; it is not a cause in any other way. How many such causes are there in the scriptures? It says there are only nine. That is to say:

> "Creation, existence, manifestation, change, cognition, attainment,
> separation, distinctness, and support—the cause is remembered as ninefold."

Among these, the mind is the cause of creation for knowledge; the purpose of the <term>puruṣa</term> is the cause of existence for the mind, just as food is for the body. The cause of manifestation...

<column-break/>

They destroy impurity through the direct and indirect paths of Yoga. "Five-fold error" is an indicator; merit and demerit are also forms of impurity, as they are the causes of birth, lifespan, and experience. The rest is easy. Because we see various types of causality, one might ask what kind of cause the practice of the limbs of Yoga is. It says: **"Practice of the limbs of Yoga,"** etc. It causes separation of the mind-stuff from impurity, so it is the "cause of separation from impurity." It provides an example: **"Just as an axe."** The axe separates the tree from its roots. By separating the mind-stuff from impurity, it leads to discriminative realization, just as merit leads to happiness. Thus, the practice of the limbs of Yoga is the "cause of attainment" of discriminative realization; it says it is not in any other way. Because of the hearing of this exclusion, one asks: **"How many are these?"** The answer: **"Only nine."** It shows them by a verse: **"That is to say—creation,"** etc.

Here, it provides examples: "Among these, the cause of creation," etc. The mind, by removing the unmanifested state and bringing the knowledge to its present state, is the cause of creation of knowledge. "Cause of existence for the mind is the purpose of the <term>puruṣa</term>." The mind, once arisen from egoism (<term>asmitā</term>), remains as long as it has not fulfilled the various purposes of the <term>puruṣa</term>. Once the two-fold purpose of the <term>puruṣa</term> is fulfilled, it departs from existence. Therefore, the unfulfilled purpose of the <term>puruṣa</term> is the cause of existence for the mind, which has arisen from its own cause. It provides an example: **"Just as for the body,"** etc.

योगं दृष्टादृष्टद्वारेणाशुद्धिं क्षिण्वन्ति । पञ्चपर्वणो विपर्ययस्येत्युपलक्षणं पुण्यापुण्ययोरपि जात्यायुर्भोगहेतुत्वेनाशुद्धिरूपत्वादिति । शेषं सुगमम् । नानाविधस्य कारणभावस्य दर्शनाद्योगाङ्गानुष्ठानस्य कीदृशं कारणत्वमित्यत आह—योगाङ्गानुष्ठानमिति । अशुद्ध्या वियोजयति बुद्धिसत्त्वमित्यशुद्धेर्वियोगकारणम् । दृष्टान्तमाह—यथा परशुरिति । परशुश्छेद्यं वृक्षं मूलेन वियोजयति । अशुद्ध्या वियोजयद्बुद्धिसत्त्वं विवेकख्यातिं प्रापयति यथा धर्मः सुखम् । तथा योगाङ्गानुष्ठानं विवेकख्यातेः प्राप्तिकारणं नान्येन प्रकारेणेत्याह—विवेकख्यातेस्त्विति । नान्यथेति प्रतिषेधश्रवणात्पृच्छति—कति चैतानीति । उत्तरम्—नवैवेति । तानि दर्शयति कारिकया—तद्यथा—उत्पत्तीति ।

अत्रोदाहरणान्याह—तत्रोत्पत्तिकारणमिति । मनो हि विज्ञानमव्यपदेश्यावस्थातोऽपनीय वर्तमानावस्थामापादयदुत्पत्तिकारणं विज्ञानस्य । स्थितिकारणं मनसः पुरुषार्थता । अस्मिताया उत्पन्नं मनस्तावत्तिष्ठते न यावद्विविधं पुरुषार्थमभिनिर्वर्तयति । अथ निर्वर्तितपुरुषार्थद्वयं स्थितेरपैति । तस्मात्स्वकारणादुत्पन्नस्य मनसोऽनागतपुरुषार्थता स्थितिकारणम् । दृष्टान्तमाह—शरीरस्येवेति । प्रत्यक्षज्ञाननिमित्त-

रागः सुखत्वे तत्त्वज्ञानं माध्यस्थ्ये । धृतिकारणं शरीरमिन्द्रियाणाम् । तानि च तस्य । महाभूतानि शरीराणां, तानि च परस्परं सर्वेषां तैर्यग्यौनमानुषदैवतानि च परस्परार्थत्वादित्येवं नव कारणानि । तानि च यथासंभवं पदार्थान्तरेष्वपि योज्यानि। योगाङ्गानुष्ठानं तु द्विधैव कारणत्वं लभत इति ॥२८॥

तत्र योगाङ्गान्यवधार्यन्ते—

### यमनियमासनप्राणायामप्रत्याहारधारणाध्यानसमाधयोऽष्टावङ्गानि ॥ २९ ॥

मूढो विषण्णो भवति चैत्रस्य मैत्रस्य पुण्यवतो बत कलत्ररत्नमेतन्न तु मम भाग्यहीनस्येति । एवं सपत्नीजनस्य तस्यां द्वेषः स्त्रीप्रत्ययस्य दुःखत्वे । एवं मैत्रस्य तस्या भर्तू रागस्तस्यैव स्त्रीप्रत्ययस्य मुखत्वे । तत्त्वज्ञानं त्वङ्मांसमेदोस्थिमज्जासमूहः स्त्रीकायः स्थानबीजादिभिरशुचिरिति विवेकिनां माध्यस्थ्ये वैराग्ये कारणमिति । धृतिकारणं शरीरमिन्द्रियाणां विधारकमिन्द्रियाणि च शरीरस्य सामान्या करणवृत्तिर्हि प्राणाद्या वायवः पञ्च तदभावे शरीरपातात् । एवं मांसादिककायाङ्गानामपि परस्परविधार्यविधारकत्वम् । एवं महाभूतानि पृथिव्यादीनि मनुष्यवरुणसूर्यगन्धर्वहशशिलोकनिवासिनां शरीराणां, तानि च परस्परं, पृथिव्यां हि गन्धरसरूपस्पर्शशब्दगुणायां पञ्च महाभूतानि परस्परं विधार्यविधारकभावेनावस्थितान्यप्सु चत्वारि तेजसि त्रीणि द्वे च मातरिश्वनीति । तैर्यग्यौनमानुषदैवतादीनि च विधार्यविधारकभावेनावस्थितानि । नन्वाधाराधेयभावरहितानां कुतस्तत्त्वमित्यत आह—**परस्परार्थत्वादिति** । मनुष्यशरीरं हि पशुपक्षिमृगसरीसृपस्थावरशरीरोपयोगेन ध्रियते । एवं व्याघ्रादिशरीरमपि मनुष्यपशुमृगादिशरीरोपयोगेन । एवं पशुमृगादिशरीरमपि स्थावराद्युपयोगेन । एवं दैवशरीरमपि मनुष्योपहृतच्छागमृगकपिञ्जलमांसाज्यपुरोडाशसहकारशाखाप्रस्तरादिभिरिज्यमानं तदुपयोगेन । एवं देवताऽपि वरदानवृष्ट्यादिभिर्मनुष्यादीनि धारयतीत्यस्ति परस्परार्थत्वमित्यर्थः । शेषं सुगमम् ॥ २८ ॥

संप्रति न्यूनाधिकसंख्याव्यवच्छेदार्थं योगाङ्गान्यवधारयति—**तत्र योगाङ्गान्यवधार्यन्त इति** । **यमनियमासनप्राणायामप्रत्याहारधारणाध्यानसमाधयोऽष्टाव-**

22½. The length of a longish quadrilateral is 120 (*dandas*) and the breadth is 40. The ditch around is as big as 4 *dandas* in breadth and 3 in depth. (Find out the cubical contents.)

The rule for arriving at the value of the cubical contents of an excavation, when the depth of the excavation varies (at various points), and also for arriving, when the cubical contents of an excavation are known, at the depth of digging necessary in the case of another (known) area (so that the cubical contents may be the same) :—

23½. The sum of the depths (measured in different places) is divided by the number of places; this gives rise to the (average) depth. This multiplied by the top area (of the excavation) gives rise to the (required) cubical contents of the excavation in the case where that area is trilateral, quadrilateral or circular. The cubical contents (of a given excavation), when divided by the (known) value of another area, gives rise to the depth (to which there should be digging, so that the resulting cubical contents may be the same).

->*Examples in illustration thereof.*<-

24½. In an equilateral quadrilateral field, the ground covered by which has an extent measured by 4 *hastas* (in length and breadth), the excavations are (in depth) 1, 2, 3, and 4 *hastas* (in four different cases). What is the measure of the average depth (of the excavations)?

25½. There is a well with an equilateral quadrilateral section, the sides whereof are 18 *hastas* in measure; its depth is 4 *hastas*. With the water of this (well), another well measuring 9 *hastas* at each of the sides (of the section) is filled. What is the depth (of this other well)?

In the case of excavations having central masses tapering upwards or downwards the operation for <term>Karmāntikaphala</term> is to add the value of half the breadth of the excavation to that of the breadth of the central mass, and for <term>Aundraphala</term>, to add the value of the breadth of the excavation to the value of the breadth of the central mass; then the procedure is as given before.

21½. The already mentioned trilateral, quadrilateral, and circular areas have ditches thrown round them. The breadth measures 80 <term>daṇḍas</term>, and the ditches are as much as 4 <term>daṇḍas</term> in breadth, and 3 <term>daṇḍas</term> in depth. Find out the cubical contents.

<note>The rule enables the calculation of the total length of a ditch in various cases. I. When the width of the ditch is uniform, the length = (d + b) × 3 for triangular/circular, or (d + b) × 4 for square, where d is the side/diameter of the central mass and b is the width of the ditch. II. When the ditch tapers, the length for <term>Karmāntika-phala</term> = (d + b/2) × 3 or 4, and for <term>Aundra-phala</term> = (d + b) × 3 or 4. These lengths must be multiplied by half the ditch width and its depth to find the cubical contents.</note>

21½. The already mentioned trilateral, quadrilateral, and circular (areas) have ditches thrown round them. The breadth measures 80 *daṇḍas*, and the ditches are as much as 4 (*daṇḍas*) in breadth, and 3 (*daṇḍas*) in depth. (Find out the cubical contents.)

and the excavation may be of the same width both at the bottom and the top, or may be of diminishing or increasing width. The rule enables us to find out the total length of the ditch in all these cases.

I. When the width of the ditch is uniform, the length of ditch = ($d + b$) × 3 in the case of an equilateral triangular or circular ditch, where $d$ is the measure of a side or of the diameter of the central mass and $b$ is the width of the ditch : but this length = ($d + b$) × 4 in the case of a square excavation with a central mass, square in section.

II. When the ditch is tapering to a point at the bottom or the top, the length of the ditch for finding out the *Karmāntika-phala* = ($d + \frac{b}{2}$) × 3, or ($d + \frac{b}{2}$) × 4, according as the central mass (1) is in section trilateral or circular, or (2) square.

Length of ditch for finding out *Aundra-phala* = ($d + b$) × 3 and ($d + b$) × 4 respectively.

These expressions have to be multiplied by half of the width of the ditch and by its depth for finding out the respective cubical *phalas*. The formulas given above in relation to triangular and circular excavations give only approximate results. With the aid of the total length of the ditch so obtained, the cubical contents are found out in the case of ditches with sloping sides by applying the rule given in stanzas 9 to 11½ above.

26½. The problems contemplated in this stanza are (a) to find out the full latitude of an inverted pyramid or cone and (b) to find out the dimensions of the cross section thereof at a desired level, when the altitude and the dimensions of the top and bottom surfaces of a truncated pyramid or cone are given. If, in a truncated pyramid with square base, *a* is the measure of a side of the base and *b* that of a side of the top surface and *h* the height, then according to the rule given here, *H* taken as the height of the whole pyramid = $\frac{a \times h}{a-b}$, and the measure of a side of the cross section of the pyramid at any given height represented by $h_1 = \frac{a (H-h_1)}{H}$.

These formulas are applicable in the case of a cone as well. In the rule the measure of the side of section forming the pointed part of the pyramid is required to be added to *H*, the denominator in the second formula, for the reason that in some cases the pyramid may not actually end in a point. Where, however, it does end in a point, the value of this side has to be zero as a matter of course.

### [Book 4]

Thus, the order of all sturdy targets for elephants, horses, and men has been told by King Someshvara, following the tradition of Jamadagni. <note>verse 135</note>

One should fill a sixteen-finger bag with goat meat. This meat should be made firm and equal to the measure of an elephant's body. <note>verse 136</note>

Dried thoroughly from the kicks of elephant and horse hooves, this firm target is called the <term>aśvakhura</term> <gloss>horse-hoof</gloss>, representing the middle of an elephant. <note>verse 137</note>

Taking the horn of a seven-year-old buffalo, fixed at the base, it is firm and equal to the body of an elephant. <note>verse 138</note>

A string five fingers high, arranged sideways, tightly bound with leather, should be made firm and equal to an elephant. <note>verse 139</note>

A tortoise-shell, round and a hand wide, should be made into a firm bone-target, equal to the measure of an elephant's limb. <note>verse 140</note>

Sixteen fingers thick, made of forest-products, wrapped with ropes, it should be made firm like the body of an elephant. <note>verse 141</note>

A wooden target, sixteen fingers wide, should be made firm and equal to the elephant's body, O King. <note>verse 142</note>

A nine-finger clay-ball on a spinning potter's wheel, made firm and bound with elephant hide, should be prepared. <note>verse 143</note>

A cotton cluster, six fingers high, bound with leather, should be made firm like an elephant's body, O King. <note>verse 144</note>

Dried cow-dung, grain, and dust, separately filled in leather, eight fingers high, should be made firm like the body of an elephant. <note>verse 145</note>

A stone, two fingers thick and sixteen fingers wide, the color of meat, should be made firm and equal to a pillar, O King. <note>verse 146</note>

<summary>This page concludes the detailed description of archery targets made of various materials, such as leather, wood, bone, and clay, modeled after the physical dimensions of elephants to train the king in precision and strength.</summary>

चतस्रः सम्पदस्त्वेतां युद्धे शत्रुनिबर्हणे ।
मृगयायां विनोदेन सोपयोगा महीपतेः ॥ ५६ ॥
चित्रं कुतूहलकरं प्रेक्षकाणां मनोहरम् ।
दर्शयेत्तदपि प्रौढ्या विनोदाय महीपतिः ॥ ५७ ॥
स्तम्भस्योपरिविन्यस्तचक्रयन्त्रे सुकीलितम् ।
वायुप्रेरितपत्रैस्तु भ्राम्यमाणं द्रुतं क्षणम् ॥ ५८ ॥
पात्रमध्ये स्थिते तोये वीक्ष्य विध्यन्विलोचने ।
प्रत्यालीढस्थितो राजा राधावेधं प्रदर्शयेत् ॥ ५९ ॥
खर्जूरीसहशाकारं कृत्वा दारुमयं तरुम् ।
नाराचैः शतशो विध्येत्स्थाने कण्टकपत्रयोः ॥ ६० ॥
पत्राणां कण्टकैश्चैव सायकैरेव कल्पयेत् ।
खर्जूरीवेधनं चित्रं प्रेयसीनां प्रदर्शयेत् ॥ ६१ ॥
वृषलं सम्मुखं कृत्वा पत्रं वक्षसि विन्यसेत् ।
तदेव तिर्यग् मोक्षेण बाणपुङ्खेन धारयेत् ॥ ६२ ॥
पत्रच्छेदमिदं चित्रं चित्तभ्रान्तिकरं नृणाम् ।
रसविस्मयमातन्वन्दर्शयेद्यदुत्तमम् ॥ ६३ ॥
एकसन्धानयुक्ताभ्यां बाणाभ्यां लक्ष्ययुग्मकम् ।
विध्यन्दर्शयेच्चित्रं यमार्जुनसंज्ञकम् ॥ ६४ ॥
अत ऊर्ध्वं स्थितं लक्ष्यमेकमोक्षेण बाणयोः ।
विकटाजुनकं चित्रं नृपो विध्यन्विनोदयेत् ॥ ६५ ॥
अर्धचन्द्राकृतीं कृत्वा तर्जन्यङ्गुष्ठतस्ततः ।
तृणकाण्डं तयोरग्रे धारितं चतुरङ्गुलम् ॥ ६६ ॥
अङ्गुल्यनुपपीतेन तद्विध्यन्नृपतिः ।
अर्धचन्द्राख्यं चित्रं दर्शयेच्च सभासदाम् ॥ ६७ ॥

**तत्सूकपाठस्तु—**

'गायत्र्यै उष्णिगुनुष्टुप् बृहती पङ्क्तिस्त्रिष्टुप् जगत्यै' ॥ १ ॥
गायत्री । उष्णिक् । अनुष्टुप् । बृहती । पङ्क्तिः । त्रिष्टुप् । जगत्यै' ॥ १ ॥

"सप्तसु छन्दःसृचः कल्पयित्वा गायत्र्यादि 'गायत्र्यै स्वाहा' इत्येवं यथाछन्दः" (शांक १८,१) इति तत्रैव शान्तিকল্পे मन्त्राणाम् ऊहनप्रकारस्य दर्शितत्वात् 'गायत्र्यै स्वाहा', 'उष्णिहे स्वाहा', 'अनुष्टुभे स्वाहा', 'पङ्क्त्यै स्वाहा', 'त्रिष्टुभे स्वाहा', 'जगत्यै स्वाहा', इत्येवम् अस्मिन् सूक्ते सप्त मन्त्रा भवन्ति । सर्वे मन्त्राः स्पष्टार्थाः ।

**इति तृतीयेऽनुवाके प्रथमं सूक्तम् ।**

'आङ्गिरसानामाद्यैः' इत्यादिसूक्तद्वयस्य 'आङ्गिरसीं गणकामस्य अभिवरनोऽभिवर्षमाणस्य च' (शांक १७,२) इति विहितायाम् आङ्गिरस्याख्यायां महाशान्तौ विनियोगः । उक्तं हि शान्तিকল্পे— "समासः" (१९,२२:२३) आङ्गिरस्याम् । 'इन्द्र मरुत्व' (अ२,५) इत्येन्द्रयाम्" (शांक १८,१;४) इति । अत्र समासशब्देन एतत् सूक्तद्वयम् उच्यते ।

<header>Atharva Veda Commentary [Hymn 20, Mantra 4</header>

The gods, who shine in the sky and possess bodies—"the wearing of armor is only for those who have bodies," hence it is said "the gods who have bodies"—they bound that armor onto their own bodies. The root <term>ṇah</term> means to bind. The middle voice is used because the fruit of the action is intended for the doer. They put it on for the sake of protecting their own bodies in the battle against the <term>asuras</term> <gloss>demons</gloss>. And the armor that <term>Indra</term> created for the sake of victory over enemies—the middle voice is used for the root <term>kṛ</term> <gloss>to do/make</gloss> as before. May that armor, worn by the gods and by <term>Indra</term> on their own bodies, protect us, who are ready for battle, from all sides against attacks made by others.

May the heaven and earth be my armor; may the day be my armor; may the sun be my armor. May all the gods make armor for me; may the hostile army never reach me. || 4 ||

May heaven and earth provide armor for me. May the day provide armor. May the sun and all the gods, including <term>Indra</term> and others, make armor for me, for the king or for me who wishes to fight. The root <term>kṛ</term> is used in the Vedic <term>luṅ</term> <gloss>aorist tense</gloss>. "May the hostile army," meaning the enemy force, being counter-intuitive or antagonistic, never reach me, the wearer of this armor. The root <term>āp</term> <gloss>to reach</gloss> is used in the <term>mā-ni</term> <gloss>prohibitive</gloss> mood. The meaning is that the enemy army should only approach the wearer of the armor in the light. Because I am wearing armor favored by the gods, I am able to kill even that enemy army.

Thus ends the eleventh hymn.
Thus ends the second <term>anuvāka</term> of the nineteenth book.

In the third <term>anuvāka</term> there are six hymns. Among them, the first hymn, "The Gayatri, the Ushnih..." is applied in the <term>Mahāśānti</term> <gloss>Great Rite of Pacification</gloss> called "Gayatri," which is prescribed for one who desires <term>brahmavarcas</term> <gloss>radiance of sacred knowledge</gloss>. It is said in the <term>Śāntikalpa</term>: "The group of meters (19.22) in the Gayatri, the collection (19.22:23) in the Agneya."

<summary>The text concludes the armor hymn by invoking heaven, earth, and the gods to protect the warrior, and introduces the ritual application of meters in the Great Rite of Pacification.</summary>

Je répondis au Priennois : Mandraïte, je
conçois et je partage ton enthousiasme ; il n'y
a que le fanatisme de la vertu et de la vérité
qui ne soit pas à craindre. Vas ! ton récit

nom de Thalès. Ton délire est tout naturel,
et le sien aussi. On ne fait rien de grand, on
n'invente rien de sublime, si l'on n'a pas la
mesure de son génie, et le sentiment de ses
forces. Thalès a raison d'être jaloux de sa
découverte ; elle est son bien ; elle est plus à
lui, que les conquêtes de Sémiramis n'étaient
à cette femme. On doit tenir à la bonne ac-
tion dont on a été capable, à une pensée
forte et hardie qu'on a su produire. La mo-
destie est la vertu de la médiocrité. Eh ! pour-
quoi ne pas se rendre justice, et la revendi-
quer pour soi comme pour les autres ?

Nous nous quittâmes à Myonte, petite ville
ionienne, à mi-chemin de Prienne à Milet.
C'est là que le Méandre, après tant de dé-
tours, tombe enfin dans la mer, et regrette
de n'en avoir pas fait encore davantage dans
une aussi agréable contrée.

Fatigué du poids de la chaleur, j'allai me
réfugier dans un vieux temple entr'ouvert,
parce que le néocore le nettoyait en ce mo-
ment. Dans le fond du sanctuaire, je distinguai,
non sans peine, à cause du peu de jour, la
statue assise d'un vieillard, recouvert d'un
long manteau fort sale. Son épaule était
chargée d'une hache poudreuse.

'Mandraite,' he said to me, with that dignity that suits men of genius, 'keep the inheritance of your fathers, to transmit it to your children. Since you press me to set a price on the three lessons you have just received on the planetary system of the world and the theory of the sun, here is what I desire from you in return: if you judge it appropriate to communicate to others what I have taught you, name the inventor of it; say to the friend whom you will instruct: Thales of Miletus, son of Examius, is the author of this system.'

O my master! I replied to him, that was indeed my intention. Yes, without doubt, I will render homage and justice to your name! Perish the ungrateful and vile disciple who dares to put himself in his master's place, and rob him of the only reward worthy of the discoveries of genius!

Thales interrupted me to say: 'Young Mandraite! forgive this weakness in an old man; I have never had any but this single ambition. It is innocent, and will cost my fellow men neither a tear nor a drop of blood. The spirit of man needs a vehicle to rise and reach the truth.'

Wise Thales! your wishes are very legitimate, and they will be fulfilled. Nature, when she judges it is time, may warn you to descend into the grave, but your name and your discoveries will not follow you there; and you can judge what posterity keeps for you, based on the honors your contemporaries have already rendered you.

Quel est ce héros, demandai-je ?

Le Néocore. C'est le dieu autochtone du pays, l'aîné de tous les autres Dieux que les Grecs nous ont fait connaître. Triple divinité ! car il préside à la fois au sentiment de l'amitié, aux vertus hospitalières, et enfin aux expiations ; et c'est sous cette dernière qualité qu'il porte une arme vengeresse et redoutable à tous ceux qui, souillés d'un crime, négligent de s'en laver.....

Pythagore. L'herbe croît sur le parvis....

Le Néocore. Les nouveaux venus font tort à l'ancien.

Pythagore. Du moins, dis-moi comment il s'appelle ?

Le Néocore. Pour les Grecs, c'est encore Jupiter. Les premiers habitans de l'Asie mineure lui donnaient un autre nom, qui s'est perdu, mais que tu pourras retrouver en voyageant jusqu'à Babylone.

Pythagore. Eh quoi ! gardien de ce temple, tu ne sais pas le nom de la divinité que tu sers ?

Le Néocore. Il me suffit que ce soit un Dieu, le père de tous les autres ; le reste m'est inutile, et doit m'être indifférent. Les immortels peuvent se passer d'avoir des noms ; mais il en faut un aux hommes qui meurent.

**75.**
And similarly, the father asked him
where he had been all day without eating.
Africo stood still for a moment,
to find a legitimate excuse for this,
which love quickly taught him,
as it is accustomed to sharpen the minds
of true lovers, and he answered his father,
and framed a lie for him in this way:

**76.**
"O my father, it is a long time since I
saw a little doe in these hills,
which was so beautiful in my opinion
that I never believe such a delightful one
was ever seen! And truly God
with His own hands made her so graceful!
And in her gait she was light as a crane,
and all white as pure snow."

**77.**
"I became so enamored that I followed her a long
distance, from wood to wood, hoping to catch her.
But she soon took the height of the mountains,
so that I remained behind with much sadness,
having given up following her further,
and in my heart I set out to find her again
and to follow her with more ease another time.
And so, returning home, I turned back."

**78.**
"I got up this morning, to tell the truth,
seeing the fine weather, I remembered
the little doe, and it came into my mind
to search for her. Thus I decided.
So I set out on a path,
that I did not notice that I found myself
halfway up the hill, when the sun was already
at the middle of the sky with its shining sphere."

**84.**
Diana le più volte va con esse

**85.**

com’ io dico il vero del suo peccato,
che, come sai, ebbe nome Mugnone,

**86.**
