The Lord of the Ocean was greatly delighted. He offered many jewels to that <term>Upasaka</term> <gloss>lay practitioner</gloss> and also sent excellent jewels to the Buddha and the <term>Sangha</term> <gloss>community of monks</gloss>. The lay practitioner and the merchants, having obtained sufficient wealth in jewels, returned safely to their own country. At that time, the lay practitioner and about five hundred merchants came to where the Buddha was staying. They bowed their heads at the feet of the Blessed One and each offered the jewels they carried. They also presented the jewels sent by the Lord of the Ocean to the Buddha and the Sangha. They knelt with their knees on the ground, joined their palms, and spoke these words to the Blessed One: "We also wish to go forth into the teachings of the Teacher." After they said this, the Blessed One said, "Come, monks!" Immediately, their hair and beards fell away, and they became monks wearing the dharma robes. Then the Blessed One taught and explained the Dharma according to their needs, whereby all their desires were exhausted and they became <term>Arhats</term> <gloss>fully awakened beings</gloss>. The great assembly rejoiced and was delighted by what the Blessed One had spoken. This is the fifth chapter, titled "The Questions of the Lord of the Ocean."

The Second Volume.
The chapter of the Son of Heaven named Gangadhara. Thus have I heard at one time: The Blessed One was staying at the Bamboo Grove, the Sanctuary of the Kalantaka Birds. At that time, there was a very great minister in that country.
<leaf-break/>
said this to him: "A great minister in the city of Rajgir is praying to me for a son. If I fulfill his prayer as he wishes, he will increase his offerings and ceremonies. If I do not fulfill his prayer, he has vowed to destroy the shrine and do something unpleasant." Since he will certainly do as he vowed, I pray you, Shakra, King of the Gods, make a son be born to him. Shakra replied: "This is indeed very difficult, but a cause is appearing right now." At that time, there was a Son of Heaven whose five virtues were fading and who was close to death. Shakra said to him: "You are close to the time of death. When you die, take birth as the son of that minister." The Son of Heaven replied: "I have faith in going forth as a monk and practicing the Holy Dharma. If I am born into a high and great family, it will be difficult to go forth. If I am born into an ordinary family, it will be easier." Shakra spoke again: "Deva, take birth there, and if you have faith in going forth, I will be your companion." That Son of Heaven then passed away and was conceived in the womb of that minister's wife within his family. Later, when he was born, he was handsome, beautiful to behold, and excellent. He was shown to the fortune-tellers, who examined him and asked, "Where was this boy first found?" They replied, "We prayed for him from the deity of the River Ganges," and thus the boy was named Gangadhara. Later, when he had grown to full stature, he spoke to his parents.

<summary>A group of merchants becomes monks after a successful voyage, followed by the beginning of the story of Gangadhara, a divine being reborn as a minister's son through the intervention of Shakra.</summary>
<keywords>Upasaka, Arhat, Shakra, Gangadhara, Rajgir, rebirth</keywords>

བ་ནི༑ སློབ་མ་དང་ཐོད་པའི་བུམ་ཆུ་རྣམས་གསང་སྦྱངས་བྱས་ཏེ། སྟོང་པའི་ངང་ལས་ཧཱུཾ་དང་རྡོ་རྗེ་ལས་མི་སྐྱོད་པ་ཡབ་ཡུམ་དུ་བསྐྱེད་པ་ལ་
ཡེ་ཤེས་པ་བཞུག །དབང་རྫས་ཀྱི་ལྷ་ཡབ་ཡུམ་སྙོམས་འཇུག་བྱས་པ་ལ་ཞུ་བ་ལས་བྱུང་པའི་ཆུར་གྱུར། དེ་ནས་སློབ་མས་བྱང་ཆུབ་རྡོ་རྗེ་
སངས་རྒྱས་ལ། ཞེས་གསོལ་བ་བཏབ་པས། བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་ཀྱི་གང་བའི་ཐོད་པ་དང་། བདུད་རྩིའི་བུཾ་པ་སྤྱི་བོར་བཞག་ནས །
རྡོ་རྗེ་དཔའ་བོ་བུམ་པའི་དབང་། དེ་རིང་ཁྱོད་ལ་བསྐུར་བར་བྱ། རྡོ་རྗེ་དཔའ་བོར་ཁྱོད་འགྱུར་ཕྱིར། བུཾ་པའི་དབང་ནི་ཁྱོད་ཀྱི་ལོང་ །
<leaf-break/>
༄༅། ༈ །ཅོད་མན་གྱི་དབང་ཐོབ་པའོ། །ང་རྒྱལ་དང་སེར་སྣའི་དྲི་མ་སྦྱངས། ཚོར་བའི་ཕུང་པོ་གནས་སུ་འགྱུར། མཉམ་པ་
ཉིད་ཀྱི་ཡེ་ཤེས་སྔོན་དུ་བྱས། རིན་ཆེན་འབྱུང་ལྡན་དུ་གྱུར་ནས་དེའི་འཕྲིན་ལས་ལ་དབང་། དེ་ནས་སློབ་མ་དང་རྡོ་རྗེ། བཛྲ་དང་པདྨ་ལས་པདྨ་
རྡོ་རྗེ་ཡབ་ཡུཾ་དུ་བསྐྱེད་ནས། རྡོ་རྗེ་གཏད་ལ། པདྨ་དཔའ་བོ་རྡོ་རྗེའི་དབང་། དེ་རིང་ཁྱོད་ལ་བསྐུར་བར་བྱ། པདྨ་དཔའ་བོར་ཁྱོད་འགྱུར་ཕྱིར།
རྡོ་རྗེའི་དབང་ནི་ཁྱོད་ཀྱི་ལོང་། པདྨ་ཨ་བྷི་ཥིཉྩ་ཧྲི། རྡོ་རྗེའི་དབང་ཐོབ་པའོ། །འདོད་ཆགས་ཀྱི་དྲི་མ་སྦྱངས། འདུ་ཤེས་གསུན་སུ་འགྱུར །
སོ་སོར་རྟོག་པའི་ཡེ་ཤེས་སྔོན་དུ་བྱས། འོད་དཔག་མེད་དུ་གྱུར་ནས་དེའི་འཕྲིན་ ལས་སྒྲུབ་པ་ལ་དབང་ངོ་། །དེ་ནས་སློབ་མ་དང་། དྲིལ་བུ་ཁ་
<leaf-break/>
༄༅། ༈ །བུདྷ་ཨ་བྷི་ཥིཉྩ་ཨོཾ། །ཀྱཻ་དཔལ་ཆེན་གེ་མོ་རྡོ་རྗེའི་གསང་མཚན་བཏགས། སོ་སོའི་བཞུག་ཏུ་ཇི་ལྟར་བལྟམས་པས་ཆུ་
དབང་བསྐུར་རོ། །མིང་གི་དབང་ཐོབ། གཏི་མུག་དྲི་མ་སྦྱངས། གཟུགས་ཕུང་གནས་འགྱུར། མེ་ལོང་ལྟ་བུའི་ཡེ་ཤེས་མངོན་དུ་བྱས །
རྣམ་སྣང་དུ་གྱུར་ཏེ། དེའི་འཕྲིན་ལས་ལ་དབང་ངོ་། དེ་ལྟར་དབང་ལྔ་ཐོབ་པས། སྤང་བྱ་མ་རིག་པ་ལྔ་སྤངས། རིག་པ་ཡེ་ཤེས་ལྔ་ཐོབ་
པས་རིག་པའི་དབང་ངོ་། དེ་ནས་སློབ་མ་ཧཱུཾ་དང་རྡོ་རྗེ་ལས་སྐྱེད་པའི་རྡོ་རྗེ་སེམས་དཔའ་ཡབ་ཡུམ་དུ་གྱུར་ཏེ། གཙོ་བོས་ཨོཾ་སརྦ་ཏ་ཐཱ་ག་
ཏ་སིདྡྷ་བཛྲ་ས་མ་ཡ་ཏིཥྛ་ཨེ་ཥ་སྟྭཾ་དྷ་རྭ་ཡ་མི་ཨོཾ་ཧི་ཧི་ཧི་ཧཱུཾ། །ཞེས་པས་རྡོ་རྗེ་ལག་པ་གཡས་པར་གཏད་དེ། སྙིང་ཁར་བཟུང་རྡོ་རྗེའི་

ཨོཾ་ཧྲི་ཧྲི་ཧཱ་ཧཱུཾ་ཧཱུཾ་ཕཊ་བཛྲ་ཨ་བྷི་ཥིཉྩ་ཧཱུཾ། མཆོད་ཆེན་ཇི་ལྟར་སྩལ་བ་ལྟར། བདག་ཀྱང་རབ་ཏུ་བསྐྱང་བའི་ཕྱིར། ནམ་མཁའི་རྡོ་རྗེ་དེང་བདག་བཅོལ་
ཆུ་དབང་ཐོབ། ཞེ་སྡང་གི་དྲི་མ་སྦྱངས། རྣམ་ཤེས་ཀྱི་ཕུང་པོ་གནས་འགྱུར། ཆོས་དབྱིངས་ཡེ་ཤེས་སྔོན་བྱས་མི་སྐྱོད་པར་གྱུར་ཏེ། དེའི་
འཕྲིན་ལས་དབང་ངོ་། །དེ་ནས་སློབ་མ་དང་ཅོད་པན། ཨཾ་དང་རིན་པོ་ཆེ་ལས། རིན་ཆེན་རྡོ་རྗེ་ཡབ་ཡུམ་དུ་སྐྱེད་ལ་ཡེ་ཤེས་པ་བཞུག་པ་
སོགས་གོང་གི་རིག་འདྲེ་ལ། དེ་ནས་ཨུ་རྒྱན་གཏད་ལ། རིན་ཆེན་དཔའ་བོ་ཨུ་རྒྱན་དབང་། དེ་རིང་ཁྱོད་ལ་བསྐུར་བར་བྱ། རིན་ཆེན་
དཔའ་བོར་ཁྱོད་འགྱུར་ཕྱིར། དབུ་རྒྱན་དབང་ནི་ཁྱོད་ཀྱིས་ལོང་། ཡི་གེ་བདུན་པའི་མཐར། རདྞ་ཨ་བྷི་ཥིཉྩ་ཏྲཾ། ཞེས་མགོ་ལ་ཀོན་ཅིང་
<leaf-break/>
ཊཾ་དང་རལ་གྲི་ལས་ཀྱི་རྡོ་རྗེ་ཡབ་ཡུམ་དུ་སྐྱེད་ལ། དེ་ནས་དྲིལ་བུ་གཏད་དེ། ལས་ཀྱི་དཔའ་བོ་དྲིལ་བུའི་དབང་། དེ་རིང་ཁྱོད་ལས་བསྐུར་བར་བྱ།
ལས་ཀྱི་དཔའ་བོར་ཁྱོད་འགྱུར་ཕྱིར་། དྲིལ་བུའི་དབང་ནི་ཁྱོད་ཀྱི་ལོང་། ཀརྨ་ཨ་བྷི་ཥིཉྩ་ཨ། དྲིལ་བུའི་དབང་ཐོབ་པའོ། །ཕྲ་དོག་དྲི་མ་སྦྱངས་
འདུ་བྱེད་གནས་གྱུར། བྱ་བ་གྲུབ་པའི་ཡེ་ཤེས་མངོན་དུ་བྱས། དོན་གྲུབ་དུ་གྱུར་ཏེ་དེའི་འཕྲིན་ལས་རབ་འབྱམས་ལ་དབང་བར་བསྒོམ་མོ།།
དེ་ནས་སློབ་མ་བྷྲཱུཾ་དང་འཁོར་ལོ་ལས་སངས་རྒྱས་མཁའ་འགྲོ་ཡབ་ཡུམ་དུ་སྐྱེད་ལ། དྲིལ་བུ་མགོ་བོར་བཞག་ནས། སངས་རྒྱས་དཔའ་བོ་
མིང་གི་དབང་། དེ་རིང་ཁྱོད་ལ་བསྐུར་བར་བྱ། སངས་རྒྱས་དཔའ་བོར་ཁྱོད་གྱུར་ཕྱིར། མིང་གི་དབང་ནི་ཁྱོད་ཀྱི་ལོང་།ཨོཾ་ཧྲི་ཧ་ཧ་ཧཱུཾ་ཧཱུཾ་
<leaf-break/>
བརྟུལ་ཤུགས་ཐོབ། སློབ་དཔོན་གྱི་དབང་སྐབས་འདིར་ཡང་རུང་། འོག་དུ་མཐར་རྟེན་རྣམས་དང་ཕྱོགས་ཅིག་པར་འབྱུང་ལ། དགེའོ།། །།
བཀྲ་ཤིས་སོ།། ༈ །།གསང་བའི་དབང་ནི་འདི་ལྟ་སྟེ། སློབ་མས་མཎྜལ་དང་དབང་བརྟེན་དུ་གསེར་ཞོ་རེ་ཕུལ་ནས་གསོལ་བ་བཏབ། བླ་མ་

I bow to the Guru and the Higher Deity. 
For those beginners who wish to perform the empowerment into the thirteen-deity mandala of Chakrasamvara and those who delight in elaborate ritual, perform the ground ritual and the deity preparation. Having invited the deities and stabilized the realization of their specificities in accordance with general practices, the preparation deities are stationed in the sky. Then, one should create the colored powder mandala.

<leaf-break/>

Then, meditate on the complete stages of the self-generation. After dissolving the retinue, if it is a cloth mandala in front, the wisdom beings are stationed in the sky. If it is a powder mandala, perform the purification into emptiness. Generate the deities through clear visualization, and before the wisdom beings reside, dissolve them into the center. 
After that, proceed up to the offerings and praises. Using the previous ritual, offer the outer tormas and perform the hundred thousand recitations. Then, just as the master bestows empowerment on the disciple, perform the self-entry. 
Following that, the disciple bathes and, outside the curtain, offers prostrations and a mandala. Having performed the preparation, asked about dreams, and so forth, the prayer is made: "You, of great joy, who embraces Vajravarahi at the throat, my teacher..."

<leaf-break/>

The essence of the awakening mind <note>term: bodhicitta</note>. Upon that, a five-pronged white vajra, radiant, is visualized. Have the disciple meditate on the awakening mind and have them say: *Om sarva yoga citta utpatayami* <gloss>Om, I generate the mind of all yoga</gloss>. 
Touching the vajra to the heart, say: *Surate samaya stvam ho! Siddha vajra yatha sukham!* <gloss>O great joy, may the pledge be firm! Accomplish the vajra according to happiness!</gloss> 
Saying *Hum* with the action vajra, lead the disciple inside the curtain. Placing the vajra on the disciple's head, the master says: "Do not disparage this; do not violate the pure pledges. You shall not go to the hell realms." By saying *Om panca amrita udka tha*, they are placed under oath. 
Then, the wisdom beings are brought down according to the mandala tradition. Saying *Om pratitstsa vajra ho*, the flower is offered and the deity is identified. Saying *Om pratigrihna hum*, the flower garland is placed on one's own head.

stored.7:
"Grant the garland." By saying *Om vajra pashe ho*, the eye-blindfold is removed and the mandala is shown.
Then, for the flask empowerment: perform the purification into emptiness for the disciple and the skull-cup flask water. From the state of emptiness, from *Hum* and a vajra, Akshobhya and consort are generated. The wisdom beings dissolve into them. The deities of the empowerment substance, male and female, enter into union, and their melting becomes the water. 
Then the disciple prays: "To the Awakening Vajra Buddha..." 
Placing the skull-cup filled with the awakening mind and the flask of nectar on the head, the master says: "Today, I shall bestow upon you the flask empowerment of the Vajra Hero. So that you may become a Vajra Hero, receive the flask empowerment!"

<leaf-break/>

The empowerment of the crown is obtained. The stains of pride and stinginess are purified. The aggregate of feeling is transformed. Mirror-like wisdom is manifest. Having become Ratnasambhava, one is empowered for his enlightened activities. 
Then, the disciple and a vajra are generated as Padma Vajra and consort from *Vajra* and *Padma*. Handing over the vajra: "Today, I shall bestow upon you the vajra empowerment of the Lotus Hero. So that you may become a Lotus Hero, receive the vajra empowerment!" 
*Padma Abhisheñca Hri*. The vajra empowerment is obtained. The stains of desire are purified. The aggregate of perception is transformed. Discriminating wisdom is manifest. Having become Amitabha, one is empowered for the accomplishment of his enlightened activities. 
Then, the disciple and a bell...

<leaf-break/>

*Buddha Abhisheñca Om*. "Kye! Great Glorious One, I give you the secret vajra name [Name]." Just as they were born at the end of each respective deity's ritual, the water empowerment is bestowed. 
The name empowerment is obtained. The stains of ignorance are purified. The aggregate of form is transformed. Mirror-like wisdom is manifest. Having become Vairochana, one is empowered for his enlightened activities. 
Thus, by obtaining the five empowerments, the five ignorances to be abandoned are discarded. By obtaining the five wisdoms of awareness, this is the empowerment of awareness. 
Then, the disciple is generated from *Hum* and a vajra into Vajrasattva and consort. The master, saying *Om sarva tathagata siddha vajra samaya tishtha esha tvam dharayami om hi hi hi hum*, hands the vajra to the right hand and holds it to the heart.
stored.8:
*Om hri hri ha hum hum phat vajra abhisheñca hum*. "Just as the great offering was granted, so that I too may be fully protected, today I entrust myself to the Vajra of Space." 
The water empowerment is obtained. The stains of anger are purified. The aggregate of consciousness is transformed. The wisdom of the sphere of reality is manifest. Having become Akshobhya, one is empowered for his enlightened activities. 
Then, for the disciple and the crown: from *Am* and a jewel, Ratnavajra and consort are generated, and the wisdom beings are dissolved into them as before. 
Then, handing over the crown: "Today, I shall bestow upon you the crown empowerment of the Jewel Hero. So that you may become a Jewel Hero, receive the crown empowerment!" 
At the end of the seven-syllable mantra, say *Ratna Abhisheñca Tram* and place it on the head.

<leaf-break/>

From *Tam* and a sword, the Karma Vajra and consort are generated. Then, handing over the bell: "Today, I shall bestow upon you the bell empowerment of the Action Hero. So that you may become an Action Hero, receive the bell empowerment!" 
*Karma Abhisheñca A*. The bell empowerment is obtained. The stains of jealousy are purified. The aggregate of mental formations is transformed. All-accomplishing wisdom is manifest. Having become Amoghasiddhi, meditate that one is empowered for his infinite enlightened activities. 
Then, the disciple is generated as the Buddha Dakini and consort from *Bhrum* and a wheel. Placing the bell on the head: "Today, I shall bestow upon you the name empowerment of the Buddha Hero. So that you may become a Buddha Hero, receive the name empowerment! *Om hri ha ha hum hum*..."

<leaf-break/>

The ascetic conduct is obtained. It is also appropriate to perform the Master empowerment at this point. Below, the concluding rituals will appear together. May it be virtuous. 
Tashi Shok <gloss>may there be auspiciousness</gloss>. 
The secret empowerment is as follows: The disciple offers a mandala and one *zho* of gold as the basis for the empowerment and makes a prayer. The Guru, with the support, assumes the pride of Chakrasamvara and consort. Inside the curtain, having blessed the vajra and lotus, the awakening mind is descended through the union of the "all-pervading," and it is given to the disciple. The near-essence mantra of the male and female deities is also recited. 
Then, saying *Aho sukha* <gloss>O, bliss!</gloss>, the disciple meditates that the channels and wheels are filled with the white and red awakening mind, and that great bliss pervades everything. By this, the stains of speech are purified. The secret empowerment is obtained. One is empowered to meditate on the completion stage of the channels, winds, and drops <term>bindu</term>.

༄༅། །རླུང་རྣམས་རྒྱུ་བ་སྟེ༐ དེ་ལྟེར་ན་རྩ་བཅུ་དང་རླུང་བཅུ་པོ་རྣམས་ནི་རྩ་སྟོང་ཕྲག་བདུན་བཅུ་རྩ་གཉིས་པ་ཐམས་ཅད་ལ་ཁྱབ་ཡོད་པར་བྱེད་པའོ།། དེ་ཡང་རྩ་
གཡོན་དང་སྣ་བུག་གཡོན་ནས་ནམཁའ་རླུང་མེ་ཆུ་སའི་རླུང་རྣམས་སྐྱེད་རིམ་ཀྱིས་རྒྱུ་ཞིང་། རྩ་གཡས་དང་སྣ་བུགཡས་ནས་ས་ཆུ་མེ་རླུང་ནམཁའི་རླུང་རྣམས་སྡུད་རིམ་ཀྱིས་རྒྱུ་སྟེ།
དེ་དག་གི་ཁ་དོག་ཀྱང་ནམཁའི་ལྗང་ཁུ་དང་། རླུང་གི་ནག་པོ་དང༐ མེའི་དམར་པོ་དང༐ ཆུའི་དཀར་པོ་དང༐ སའི་སེར་པོ་ཡིན་ཅིང་།། འབབ་པའི་ལམ་དང་ཚད་ནི༐ སའི་རླུང
ནི་སྣ་བུག་གཉི་ཀའི་འོག་གི་ཕྱོགས་ནས་སོར་བཅུ་གཉིས་ཕྱི་རོལ་དུ་འགྲོ་ཞིང་༐ ནང་དུ་ལྟེ་བའི་འོག་ཏུ་སོར་བཞི་འགྲཽ།། ཆུའི་རླུང་ནི་སྣའི་ཀ་བའི་ཕྱོགས་ནས༐ ཕྱི་རོལ་དུ་སོར་
བཅུ་གསུམ་འགྲོ་ཞིང༐ ནང་དུ་ལྟེ་བའི་འོག་དུ་སོར་གསུམ་འགྲཽ།། མེའི་རླུང་ནི་སྣའི་ཕྱི་རོལ་གྱི་ཕྱོགས་ནས་ཕྱི་རོལ་དུ་སོར་བཅུ་བཞི་འགྲོ་ཞིང༐ ནང་དུ་ལྟེ་པའི་འོག་ཏུ་སོར་གཉིས
འགྲཽ།། རླུང་གི་རླུང་ནི་སྣའི་སྟེང་གི་ཕྱོགས་ནས་ཕྱི་རོལ་དུ་སོརབཅོའ་ལྔ་འགྲོ་ཞིང༐ ནང་དུ་ལྟེ་(྾)བའི་པད་མ་ཉིད་ནས་ལྡོགོ། ཡེ་ཤེས་ཀྱི་རླུང་ནི་སའི་དཀྱིལ་འཁོར་གྱི་མཐར་
<leaf-break/>
༄༅། །ལ་དཀྱིལ་འཁོར་རྣམས་ཞེས་པའོ།། ཞེས་པ་ལྟར༴ ཞགཅིག་གི་ཆུ་ཚོད་དྲུག་བཅུའི་དུས་ལ༴ དབུགས་འབྱུང་བ་དང་འཇུག་པ་ཉི་ཁྲི་ཆིག་སྟོང་དྲུག་རྒྱ་རྒྱུ་བ་ལྶ༴
ལྟེ་བའི་རྩ་འདབ་བཅུ་གཉིས་ཀྱི་འདབ་མ་རེ་རེ་ལ་འཕོའ་ཆེན་ནམ་དུས་སྦྱོར་གཅིགི་དབུགས་སྟོང་བརྒྱད་བརྒྱ་དང༴ ཆུ་ཚོད་ལྔ་ལྔ་རྒྱུ་བས་འཕོ་བ་བཅུ་གཉིས་སུ་འགྱུར་ཞིང ༴
དེ་ཡང་གཡོན་གྱི་རྩ་འདབ་དྲུག་ལ་རྒྱུ་བ་ན་རླུང་སྣ་བུག་གཡོན་ནས་རྒྱུ་ཞིང༴ གཡས་ཀྱི་རྩ་འདབ་དྲུག་ལ་རྒྱུ་བ་ན༴ རླུང་སྣ་བུག་གཡས་ནས་རྒྱུ་བ་སྟེ༴ དུས་སྦྱོར་རེ་རེ་གཡོན་དང་
གཡས་སུ་འཕོ་བའི་ཚུལ་གྱིས་སོ།། དེ་ལྟར་གཡོན་ནས་གཡས་དང་གཡས་ནས་གཡོན་དུ་འཕོ་བའི་འཚམས་སུ༴ དབུགས་འབྱུང་(བ)དང་འཇུག་པ་ལྔ་བཅུ་རྩ་དྲུག་དང་བཞི་ཆ་རེ
རྩ་དབུ་མའི་ནང་དུ་རྒྱུ་ཞིང་། དེའི་ཚེ་རླུང་སྣ་བུག་གཉིས་ལ་མཉམ་པོར་རྒྱུ་ལ། ཞག་གཅིག་གི་དབུ་མའི་དབུགས་ནི་དྲུག་རྒྱ་དང་བདུན་བཅུ་རྩ་ལྔར་འགྱུར་ཏེ། དབང་མདོར་བསྟན་
པར༴ དུས་སྦྱོར་འཆར་བའི་མངོན་འཚམས་སུ།། དབུ་མ་ནས་ནི་མཉམ་པར་འབབ།། རྐང་པ་དང་བཅས་ལྔ་བཅུ་དྲུག། ༔ མདོར་ན་རྩ་སྟོང་ཕྲག་བདུན་བཅུ་རྩ་གཉིས་པོ་
འབྱུང་དང་འཇུག་པའི་མི་ཡི་བདག། བདུན་བཅུ་རྩ་ལྔས་ལྷག་པ་ཡི།། དྲུག་རྒྱ་ཉིད་དང་མཚན་ལའོ།། ཞེས་གསུངས་པ་I
<leaf-break/>
༄༅། །པ་བ་སངས་དང་༴ སྤེན་པ་དང་༴ མཇུག་རིངས་རྣམས་སུ་གསུངས་ཞིང་། དེས་ན་སྐབས་འདིར་སྟེང་གི་གཟའ་དེ་རྣཾས་བཅིང་ཞིང་ཕྱི་ནས་འོག་གི་གཟའ་
གསུམ་པོ་ཡང་བཅིང་བར་བྱའོ་ཞེས་པ་སྟེ། དང་པོ་བསྒྲུབ་པའི་གནས་བརྟག་པ་ནི། རྩ་བའི་རྒྱུད་ལས༴ གང་དུ་ས་སྐྱོང་ཆོས་ལྡན་ཞིང་།། གང་ཞིག་ཁོ་ནར་སྐྱེ་དགུ་རྣམས།།
བདེར་གནས་ས་འཛིན་རྩོད་མེད་པ།། དེར་ནི་བསྒྲུབ་པ་བརྩམ་པར་བྱ།། ཞེས་གསུངས་པས༴ སྡེ་འཁྲུག་དང་འཐབ་བརྩོད་མེད་ཅིང་། མི་དང་མི་མ་ཡིན་གྱི་རྒྱུན་སྲང་མ་
ཟུག་པའི་གནས་སུ། བླ་མ་དང་གཙུག་ལག་ཁང་ལ་སོགས་པའི་ལོག་འཚོ་སྤངས་པའི་ཡོ་བྱད་བསོགས་ནས། སྒོམ་ཁང་རང་བཞིན་གྱིས་མུན་པ་གནག་ཅིང་། ཕུགས་སུཾ་
རིམ་པ་ལྟ་བུའཾ། མདོར་ན་དཔངས་མཐོ་བ་ཞལ་ཞལ་བྱས་པ། སྒོ་ཁྱོག་རིམ་པ་གསུམ་དང་ལྡན་པ། སྣང་བ་ཁབ་རྩེ་ཙམ་ཡང་མེད་པའི་ནང་དུ། བདེ་བའི་སྟན་ལ་འདུག་

This is taught as a branch of the Great Accomplishment. Regarding that, first is the preliminary practice of the Body Vajra, which purifies the channels of the body. One practices by means of the three cross-legged postures. By the upper cross-legged posture, one binds the upper channels. By the lower cross-legged posture, one binds the lower channels. By the middle cross-legged posture, one binds the middle channels. 
By relying on the binding of those channels, the winds are bound. By relying on the binding of those winds, the <term>bindu</term> <gloss>essence</gloss> of <term>Bodhicitta</term> <gloss>awakened mind</gloss> is bound. By relying on that binding, one should know that the <term>samadhi</term> <gloss>meditative absorption</gloss> of bliss, clarity, and non-conceptuality is born.
It is said: "The essence of the seventy-two thousand channels is firmly bound like the planets in the expanse of space." In this body endowed with the six elements, seventy-two thousand channels are formed. Furthermore, first in the mother's womb, the semen, blood, and the consciousness of the <term>bardo</term> <gloss>intermediate state</gloss> are blessed by bliss. Then, after one month, in the center of the heart, ten channels about the size of an extremely fine hair-tip are formed, which serve as the support for the ten life-sustaining winds. From then on, the channels increase by two hundred each day. At twelve months, they reach the number of seventy-two thousand.

<leaf-break/>

Three are the elements of earth, wind, and gnosis that flow. Water, wind, and space are the branches of method, while earth and fire are gnosis, the branch of wisdom; in this manner, they perfectly abide in all embodied beings. These six channels are the root of all the seventy-two thousand channels said to abide in the body.
Regarding the manner in which those channels abide above and below: from the Glorious <term>Kalachakra</term> <gloss>Wheel of Time</gloss>, it is said: "The <term>nada</term> <gloss>subtle resonance</gloss>, the <term>bindu</term> <gloss>drop</gloss>, the <term>kala</term> <gloss>part</gloss>, and the gnosis which has reached the place of nectar: these are the channels bound in a chain-link. The three paths of the life-sustaining and downward-clearing winds, together with the 'vajra,' the 'lotus-vajra,' and the 'water-born' <note>referring to the secret organs</note>." 
Among the six wheels of the body: <term>nada</term> refers to the heart chakra; <term>bindu</term> refers to the forehead chakra; <term>kala</term> refers to the throat chakra; "gnosis" refers to the navel chakra. Those reaching the "place of nectar" are the three upper channels that go from the navel to the forehead, and from the forehead to the <term>ushnisha</term> <gloss>crown protuberance</gloss>. From the navel to the heart, they exist in the form of three paths, and from the heart to the throat, also...

<leaf-break/>

...the channel of [feces] goes through the center, the channel of urine goes through the right, and the <term>Dungchenma</term> <gloss>Conch-like One</gloss> goes through the center. These three channels also move by forming three paths. Below the chakra of the secret place, the channel of excrement goes through the center, the channel of urine goes through the left, and the channel of semen goes through the right.
The channel-petals of the six chakras branch out from the two channels of the Sun and Moon in their respective locations, like branches of a tree. From those, they further divide into many subtle channel-petals, totaling seventy-two thousand. The central <term>Avadhuti</term> channel abides in the center of the wheels like a hub, without channel-petals. However, it is said that from the <term>ushnisha</term> it branches into many petals like the shape of a parasol, pervading the entire body. 
Regarding how the winds move through those channels: simultaneously with the formation of the ten heart channels, the petals in the East and South-East, and those above and below, move in sequence: the "equally-abiding," the "upward-moving," the "pervading," the "naga," the "tortoise," the "lizard," the "Devadatta," the "Dhananjaya," and the "life-sustaining" and "downward-clearing" winds.

པར་གསལ་ཞིང་༐ ཡིད་ཆེས་པར་མཐོང་བ་ཡིན་ནོ།། རྒྱུ་དེའི་ཕྱིར་བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའ་དོན་གྲུབ་ཀྱིས། ཐོ་རངས་བདུད་བཅོམ་པར་བྱས་སོ་ཞེས་གསུངས་པའོ།།
བཅོམ་ལྡན་འདས་ཀྱིས་དམ་བཅའ་བ་མཛད་པར་ཡང་༐ བསམ་པ་ཐམས་ཅད་ཡོངས་སྤངས་ནས།། ཉི་མ་གཅིག་ནི་ཡོངས་སུ་བརྟག། གལྟེ་རྟགས་ནི་མ་བྱུང་ན།། དེ་ཚེ་ང་ཡི་རྫུན་ཚིག་ཡྣི་།།
ཅེས་པས༐ འཇིག་རྟེན་པའི་དངོས་གྲུབ་སྒྲུབ་པ་ལ་ནི་ཉིན་མཚན་གཅིག་གིས་རྟགས་མཐོང་བ་མེད་དོ།། དེའི་ཕྱིར་ལམ་རིན་པོ་ཆེ་འདི་ནི་ཤིན་དུ་ངོ་མཚར་ཞིང་རྙེད་པར་དཀའ་བས་
གསང་ཞིང་ཉམས་སུ་བླང་བར་བྱའོ།། དེ་ཡང་སྒོམ་ཁང་གི་ནང་གི་མུན་པའི་སྣང་བ་དེ་ཉིད་ལ་མིགི་དབང་པོ་དང༐ ཤེས་པ་རོ་མཉམསུ་ཁྱབ་པར་བཀོད་ནས། ཁ་ཟས་ཀྱི་བྱ་བའི
དུས་མ་གཏོགས་པ་ཐུན་འཚམས་མེད་པར་སྒོམ་པའོ།། ཁ་ཟས་ཀྱི་དུས་སུ་ཡང་མིགི་ལྟ་སྟངས་དང་སེམས་ཀྱི་འཇོག་ཐབས་མ་ཤོར་བར་བྱའོ།། གལ་ཏེ་ཐུན་འཚམས་ཅུང་ཟད
<leaf-break/>
༄༅། །ཞེས་གསུངས་ཏེ་༐ སེམས་ཀྱི་མཉམ་པར་འཇོག་ཚུལ་ཐུན་མོང་མ་ཡིན་པ་འདི་ལྟ་བུའི་ཚུལ་གྱིས་མཉམ་པར་གཞག་པ་ན ། རྡོེའི་མེ་དང་དུ་བ་ཞེས་པ་ཆོས
ཉིད་འོད་གསལ་བ་ལྷན་གཅིག་སྐྱེས་པའི་ཡེ་ཤེས་ཀྱི་ངོ་བོར་གྱུར་པའི་མེ་དང་དུ་བ་ལ་སོགས་པ་གསལ་བར་སྣང་ཞིང་། དེ་ལྟ་བུའི་ངང་ནས་ལུས་སེམས་ཁོང་ཀློད་ལ་བསྒོམ་པར་བྱ་སྟེ།
བྲམ་ཟེ་ཆེན་པོའི་ཞལ་ནས། འཇུར་བུས་བཅིངས་པའི་སེཾས་ཉིད་ནི།། ཀློད་ན་གྲོལ་བར་ཐེ་ཚོམ་མེད།། ཅེས་གསུངས་པའོ།། རྣལ་འབྱོར་གྱི་དབང་ཕྱུག་ཏེ་ལོ་པའི་ཞལ་ནས་ཀྱང་༐
སེཾས་ནི་ནམཁའི་དཀྱིལ་ལྟར་བསམ་ཡུལ་འདས།། དེ་དང་བཏང་བཞག་མེད་པར་ཀློད་ལ་ཞོག། སེཾས་ལ་གཏད་སོ་མེད་ན་ཕྱག་ཆེན་ཡིན།། དེ་ལ་གོམས་པས་བླ་མེད་བྱང་ཆུབ
ཐོབ །། ཅེས་གསུངས་པས་༐ ལུས་སེཾས་ཁོང་ཀློད་པའི་ངང་ནས་ལྟ་སྟངས་དང་༐ ཤེས་པ་ནམཁའ་དང་དབྱེར་མེད་དུ་ཟང་ཐ་ལེ་འཇོག་པའོ།། དཔལ་ཀྱེའི་རྡོ་རྗེའི་རྒྱུད་དུ་ཡང་༐
ཀུན་མཁྱེན་གོ་འཕང་འདོད་པ་ཡིས།། རྟོག་པ་རྣམ་པ་སྣ་ཚོགས་པ།། དེ་ཀུན་གང་ལ་མེད་གྱུར་པ།། དེ་ལ་རྟག་ཏུ་བརྩོན་པར་བྱ །། ཞེས་པ་དང་༐ འཕགས་པ་བསྡུད་པ་ལས་ཀྱང་།

stored.15:
...The winds move. In that way, the ten channels and the ten winds pervade all seventy-two thousand channels. Furthermore, through the left channel and left nostril, the winds of space, wind, fire, water, and earth move in the order of the generation stage. Through the right channel and right nostril, the winds of earth, water, fire, wind, and space move in the order of the completion stage. 
Their colors are also: green for space, black for wind, red for fire, white for water, and yellow for earth. Regarding the path and measure of their flow: the earth wind moves twelve finger-widths outward from the lower part of both nostrils and moves four finger-widths inward below the navel. The water wind moves thirteen finger-widths outward from the side of the nasal bridge and moves three finger-widths inward below the navel. The fire wind moves fourteen finger-widths outward from the outer side of the nose and moves two finger-widths inward below the navel. The wind-element wind moves fifteen finger-widths outward from the upper part of the nose and turns back right from the navel lotus. The gnosis wind, at the end of the earth mandala...

<leaf-break/>

...it is said "the mandalas." Accordingly, during the sixty <term>chu-tsod</term> <gloss>Tibetan hours</gloss> of one day, the exhalations and inhalations move twenty-one thousand six hundred times. For each of the twelve petals of the navel chakra, there is one "great shift" or "zodiacal sign" <note>Sanskrit: lagna</note> consisting of one thousand eight hundred breaths. As it moves for five <term>chu-tsod</term> each, there are twelve shifts. 
Furthermore, when moving through the six left petals, the wind moves through the left nostril. When moving through the six right petals, the wind moves through the right nostril. This occurs in the manner of shifting between left and right for each zodiacal period. At the transition of shifting from left to right and right to left, fifty-six and a quarter breaths move within the central channel. At that time, the wind moves equally through both nostrils. In one day, the breaths in the central channel total six hundred and seventy-five. 
As stated in the *Brief Introduction to the Empowerment*: "At the precise transition of the rising zodiacal sign, it flows equally from the central channel; fifty-six with a quarter [breaths]." In short, regarding the seventy-two thousand channels: "The lord of humans, [during] the exiting and entering, [it is] six hundred and seventy-five [breaths] more [for the central channel] during day and night." Thus it is said.

<leaf-break/>

...Jupiter, Venus, Saturn, and the "Long-tail" <note>Ketu/Comet</note> are mentioned. Therefore, at this stage, those upper planets are bound, and subsequently, the three lower planets should also be bound. 
First, regarding the examination of the place for accomplishment: the *Root Tantra* says: "Where the protector of the land is righteous, and where living beings alone abide in happiness without dispute over the land, there one should begin the accomplishment." Thus, in a place without civil strife or conflict, where the paths of humans and non-humans do not cross, one should gather provisions abandoned of wrong livelihood such as from gurus or temples. The meditation room should be naturally dark, with three levels in the back, or at least with high walls and plastered. Inside a room with a three-staged crooked door and not even a needle-tip of light, sit on a comfortable cushion and generate the supreme mind of enlightenment. Practice Guru Yoga and pray fervently. Then, initially, when the life-breath descends into the right channel, place the mind in space and meditate.
stored.16:
When [the breath] flows, it is consistent with the earth wind. When it flows at the end of the space wind, it is consistent with the space wind. 
The functions of the ten winds mentioned previously are as follows: the life-sustaining wind, which is the nature of the Moon and Sun, performs the support. The downward-clearing wind draws down the food and drink of the six tastes. The equally-abiding wind equalizes the essence of the seven constituents. The upward-moving wind performs the actions of the "naga" <note>coughing</note>, laughter, speaking, and so on, as well as spontaneous dancing and movement. The pervading wind performs jumping, running, opening, and moving. The "naga" wind performs belching. The "tortoise" wind performs the contraction of the legs and arms. The "lizard" wind performs all anger and agitation. The "Devadatta" wind performs yawning. The "Dhananjaya" wind prevents the dead body from decaying. 
Regarding that, the life-sustaining wind: in the *Brief Introduction to the Empowerment*, the sequential flow of <term>chu-tsod</term> is: "Three hundred breaths with sixty; eighteen hundred breaths, those move in the former <term>chu-tsod</term>." For the sixty <term>chu-tsod</term> of day and night, in the body...

<leaf-break/>

The essence of [the channels] is the wind and the <term>Alaya-vijnana</term> <gloss>storehouse consciousness</gloss>, which is the Bodhicitta. The former is the support, and the latter is the supported. Because these are not bound, there are the "four states of samsara." They are also called the "four great leaking gates of samsara." Because one is liberated from samsara by binding them in sequence, they are called "binding." 
Where should they be bound? In the "expanse of space." They are bound by the two yogas of the space of darkness and the space of light. How should they be bound? By "stability," which means binding without movement, such that the object and the subject do not enter into one another. Here, "planets" refers to the gates of the senses. From the *Stainless Light*: "Here, the rectum, the urinary path, the semen path, the mouth, the right eye, the left eye, the right nostril, the left nostril, the right ear, and the left ear are respectively: the Moon, the Sun, Rahu, Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus, Saturn, and Ketu." This is what is taught. Therefore, at this stage, one should bind those upper planets and then later bind the three lower planets.

<leaf-break/>

Set the mind in space and meditate. This is not done when [the breath] flows in the left channel, because that would generate space and so forth. Regarding the physical posture: cross the legs, straighten the spine, and press the channels of the two thighs with the two hands formed into vajra-fists. Pull the two shoulders back slightly toward the nape. Bend the neck slightly so the chin presses against the throat-lock. With the "wrathful gaze of the wheel-holder," look upward without moving. 
Because the body, mind, and wind are dependent on one another, if the physical posture is distorted, the key points of wind and mind will also be distorted. Therefore, if one knows how to adopt the cross-legged posture correctly, the "wind of wind," which is the downward-clearing wind of the secret place, is bound. By placing the fists on the top of the thighs and straightening the abdomen, the equally-abiding fire wind is bound. By spreading the shoulders like the wings of a vulture and keeping the chest neither too bent nor too upright, the life-holding water wind in the heart is bound. Like bridling a swift horse, by pressing the chin to the throat-lock...

བཟངས་པོ་ཡིས་། བསྡུག་པོ་བཀོད་པའི་གནས་སུ་བཟུང་། དེ་ནས་ལྟང་ལོ་ཅན་གྱི་གནས་། ཀུན་རིག་རྣམ་པར་སྣང་མཛད་ཀྱི། འདི་ཉིད་བཟུང་པས་རིགས་ལྔར་སྨིན། དེ་འདས་ང་ཡི་བཟུང་པ་ཡིས་། བསྟན་པ་སྫོགས་ཤིང་དབང་
པ་ཡི། སདྱས་སྟོང་དང་རྩ་གཉིས་ནི། འདི་ལ་བརྟེནས་ངེས་པར་འབྱུང་། རྫུས་དང་སྒོ་ང་ལས་སྐྱེས་དང་། དྲོད་དང་མངལ་ནས་སྐྱེས་པ་ཡི། སེཾན་རྣམས་ནི་སྨིན་པར་བྱེད། འདུལ་༤་བསྟན་པ་འདི་ཉིད་ནས་། བཅུ་གཉིས་ཆོས་ཀྱི་
འཁོར་ལོར་འབྱུང་། འདི་ཡི་མཛད་པ་སུམ་བཅུ་དྲུག། སྐུ་གསུང་ཐུགས་ལ་བརྟེནས་ནི། གདུལ་ཡུལ་སེཾན་རྣམས་ལ་གནང་། ང་ནི་མྱ་ངན་འདས་འོག་ཏུ། ནུབ་ཕྱོགས་དབུའ་རྒྱན་དག་གི་ཡུལ་། འདའ་ན་ཀོ་ཤའི་ལྷ་ལྕམ་ལ་། ཕ

༄༅།། །།ཚ་བུར་དཀར་སྦྱར་བའི་ཕྱེ་མ་ལ།། རྩམ་པ་མ་ཞུ་ཕབས་དང་བུལ་སྡོག་སྣན།། ཤ་མ་ཞུ་ན་སྤྱང་ཁུའི་ཕོ་བ་ནམ། ས་
པོ་གྱ་རྒོད་ཀྱི་གྲེ་བ་སྣན་མ་སྟོང་།། ཤ་ཁུ་ལ་སོགས་པའི་ཐང་དང་ལྟག་པ་སྤྲད།། སྔོ་དང་མ་ཞུ་ཟ་དང་སྦྱི་མོང་སྣན།། ཆང་མ་ཞུ་ན་ཕབས་སྣན་ཆང་
བསྐོལ་བ་སྟོང་།། ཡང་ན་བསོགས་ཚིགས་ཐང་པའི་འཇུ་བར་བྱེད།། ཇ་ཆུ་མ་ཞུ་ཚ་སྣན་དྲི་ཆུ་སྟོང་།། ཞོ་དར་འོ་མ་མ་ཞུ་ཆུར་ལུས་འཇུ།།
མར་ཚིལ་མ་ཞུ་ལྕོང་ཞི་མ་སྟུལ་སྣན།། འབྲུ་མར་མ་ཞུ་སྲན་ཕྱེ་ལྟག་སྤྲད་འགམ།། རྡོ་མ་ཞུ་ལ་འཚུར་དང་ཟེ་ཚ་སྣན།། སྨས་མ་
ཁུ་བ་སུག་རིལ་ལྟག་པ་སྤྲད།། སྨན་རྗེས་སོ་ཆ་ཤུ་དག་པི་ལི་ལིང་།། སྒ་སྐྱ་རའི་འོ་མས་གྱེན་དུ་སྡང་།། ནད་རྡག་དང་པོར་སྐྱུགས་བྱ་རྗེས་ལ་
སྨན།། ཁྱད་པར་ཚ་དུགས་ཆུ་སྐོལ་རྩོལ་སྤྱད་མཆོག། དངས་མ་མ་ཞུ་ཆ་སྙམ་བཞི་ཐང་སྟོང་།། བྱེར་ན་འོ་མ་ལན་ཚ་བཏབ་པས་བསྡུས།།

<leaf-break/>
༄༅།། །།ཀན་ལྡན་པ་སློན། རང་རང་ཁ་འཛིན་ཟས་སྨན་འཚལ་བས་བཅོས། མ་ཞུ་སྙིངས་ནས་ནད་གཞན་འགྱུར་བ་ལ། དང་

འབྱུང་། ཅེས་གསུངས་སོ། ། དེ་ནས་དྲང་བ་སྲོངས་ཡིད་ལ་སྐྱེས་ཀྱིས་འདི་སྐད་ཞུས་པ། ཀྱེ་བསྟོན་པ་དྲང་བསྲོངས་རིག་པའི་ཡེ་ཤེས་ལགས། །
མ་ཞུའི་རྒྱུས་བསྐྱེད་འབྲས་བུའི་ལྕོང་ནད་དུ། དེ་དག་རྒྱུ་རྐྱེན་གྱུར་ཚུལ་དབྱེའ་བ་དང་། རྟགས་དང་བཅོས་ཐབས་རྗེས་བཅོད་ཇི་ལྟར་བགྱིའ།

...and at unsuitable times. Regarding the types of food, they are categorized as hard, soft, oily, and processed. Hard refers to raw vegetables or tough meat. Soft refers to beer, water, milk, and curd. Oily refers to butter, grain oil, fat, and marrow. Indigestion from oils and processed foods causes the greatest harm. The types are divided into the indigestion of the clear essence <term>dangs-ma</term> and the indigestion of the waste <term>snyigs-ma</term>. The latter is called "waste indigestion." When food is not digested in its own place within the stomach, Phlegm and mucus increase, wrapping and holding the food. This results in "food tumors" from the massing of waste. If the Wind that resides in the stomach fails to separate the clear essence from the waste, the waste enters the channels of the clear essence. Then, because the Bile does not mature the blood and constituents, the signs of "old indigestion" <term>ma-zhu rnying-pa</term> appear. The clear essence may spread, stagnate, mass, or leak. Leaking causes "pale disease" <term>skya-rbabs</term> <gloss>edema/anemia</gloss> and an increase in Phlegm. Spreading causes conditions like poisoning, leprosy, "fire-snake" <gloss>shingles/erysipelas</gloss>, tumors, sores, gout, jaundice, channel-tumors, and "elephant foot." Stagnation leads to **Brown Phlegm**, "hidden fever," and spleen disease. Most diseases are produced by the indigestion of the clear essence.

<leaf-break/>

Chronic indigestion is the cause of all ailments. Indigestion is called the "demon disease" because the mucus blocks the downward-clearing path and turns it upward. This causes the internal passages to be narrow and the breath to be obstructed. It results in sour belching, hiccups, and the stomach feeling full. At night it is painful, and eventually it turns into **Brown Phlegm** or jaundice. Indigestion is said to be "like wood" because the mucus blocks the paths of the upward and downward-moving Winds. The digestive fire is lost, the stomach is distressed, and the disease enters the channels. The body cannot bend or stretch, feeling as if a piece of wood were inside. Wherever the disease settles, there is sharp pain and colic <term>glang-thabs</term>. When the clear essence from indigestion spreads into the channels, it sticks to the channel walls. Like a poison, the flesh and body turn blue and pale. Strength is low, one feels unwell after eating, and the appetite is poor. One cannot tolerate either heat or cold. If the indigestion is accompanied by Wind, there is shivering, trembling, and dizziness in the limbs. If accompanied by Bile, there is internal heat, foul-smelling yellow diarrhea, much belching, vomiting, thirst, and fever. If accompanied by Phlegm, there is much sticky saliva, the body feels heavy, the mind is submerged, and food is tasteless.

<leaf-break/>

Indigestion eventually turns into the poison of the waste products. This is because the clear essence resides in the liver and has the heat of Bile, while the waste resides in the stomach and is combined with Phlegm and Wind. For moderate indigestion, use a decoction of "King Salt" <term>rgyal-tsha</term> and the "Four Salts." Use "King Salt," black salt, and the "Three Hot Meds" <note>ginger, long pepper, black pepper</note>. A hot decoction of these creates warmth and digests the indigestion. To pacify it, use "Mouth of the Wild Mare" powder <note>rgod-ma-kha</note>, or pomegranate with the "Five Hot Meds" and the "Three Salts." Deliver a small dose of "White Purge" <term>thar-nu</term> powder with hot water. If the dose is too large, it will become an ally to the mucus and make digestion even harder. Apply heat using stones or clods of earth. This draws out the "vapor" of the indigestion and induces sweat. For great indigestion, use purges after the medicine has been digested. If the disease is in the upper body, induce vomiting; if in the lower body, use a medicinal enema <term>ni-ru-ha</term>. If in the middle, use a laxative. Afterwards, if food and behavior are incorrect, the disease will increase again. Therefore, be extremely careful with diet and behavior following the treatment. If the root is not removed despite these efforts, apply moxibustion or a lancet to the stomach points. Specifically, for waste indigestion, increase the stomach heat with pomegranate and the "Three Hot Meds." To digest the indigestion, use "King Salt," black salt, and white salt.

འགྱུར་འཕེལ་འགྲིབ་བྱེད་པ་ཡིན།། སྔལ་སྙན་ཚིགས་པས་རྒྱུ་ཞབས་ལྡང་དུབ་གཟེར།། འགྲངས་ཚེ་ན་ཞིང་སྐབསུ་ཁྲག་ཅན་འཛག། །།
སྒངས་པའི་རྗེ་སྙན་ཆུ་སྒོག་ཟུག་གཟེར་ཆེ།། གློའི་རྩ་སྙན་གློ་ལང་སྒོག་པ་བཀའ །། སྐད་འཛེར་ཤ་ལུས་སྔོ་བཀམས་ཟོས་རྗེས་སྐྱུག། མཁན་
མའི་རྩ་སྙན་ཐོག་མར་ན་ཟུགས་ཆུང།། སྨིན་ནས་ལྟར་སྔོན་ཤ་བཀམ་དགྱེད་དགུག་བཀའ།། ཆུ་མདོག་དམར་ལ་འདུས་ལྕི་ཆུ་འཐུང་སྐྱུག།མཆིན
གྲི་རྩ་སྙན་ཚིགས་པ་བརྒྱད་པ་ན།། དགྱེད་དགུག་མི་བདེ་སྒེག་ཅིང་སྐྱུག་སྙམ་བྱེད།། མཆིན་པ་འཆིན་གྲིའི་གཟོས་སྐྱུག་པར་འགྱུར།། རྩ་སྙན་
ཕལ་ཆེར་རིལ་རྩམ་རྩ་ཆུ་ཚ།། སྲིན་སྙན་འདྲིལ་དུས་ཟུགས་ཆེ་ཞི་དུས་མེད།། ཡུ་སྙན་གང་དུ་བྱུང་པའི་གནས་རྟགས་བསྟོན།། སྙིང་གི་
<leaf-break/>
༄༅།། །།པོ་ནང་ན་གནས་པའི་ཚ་སྐན་ལ།། ཏིག་ཏ་གསེར་ཀྱི་མེ་ཏོག་དུག་མོ་སྙུངས།། བསིལ་བསུམ་ཤག་ཞུན་ཏུ་ཧ་པི་པི་ལིང།།
ཚ་ལ་ཨ་རུ་ར་དང་འགྲོན་ཐལ་དང།། ལྕོང་ཞི་དྲག་པོས་སྟུལ་བའི་ཐལ་བ་དང།། ལྡོང་རོས་ཧོང་ལེན་ད་ལིས་ཐལ་བ་རྣམས།། ཀ་ར་སྦྱར་སྟང་གང་
ཉེའི་རྩ་ལ་སྟར།། རྩ་ལྟོ་གང་རིགས་སྦྱར་ལ་ཆུ་ལུམས་བྱ།། བར་གནས་ཚ་སྐན་བཟང་དྲུག་ཨ་རུ་ར།། རྩན་དན་དཀར་དམར་ཨུད་དཔལ་
བོང་དཀར།། ཏིག་ཏ་གསེར་ཀྱི་མེ་ཏོང་དུག་མོ་སྙུངས།། རུ་རྟ་ཚ་ལ་དྱལ་ཚ་པི་པི་ལིང།། སྤོས་དཀར་གསེང་ལྡན་མུ་ཟི་སེ་རུ་དང།། རྟ་མིག
རྩང་མ་ཅན་གཟན་རུས་པ་དང།། ག་པག་རྒོད་རྭ་དང་ར་རུས་གསེར་ཙམ་བསྲེགས།། ལྕོང་ཞི་རྒོ་སྟུལ་ཀ་ར་སྦྱར་ལ་སྟང།། གཏར་སྦྱངས་ཆུ་ལུམས་
གོང་བཞིན་གཤེགས་པར་བྱ།། ཕྱིའི་ཚ་སྐན་འཁན་པ་དཔྱང་ཚེར་རྩ།། ལྕེ་ཚ་འོལ་མོ་གོ་སྙོད་བྱི་ལའི་བྲུན།། སྦང་ལུམས་བྱས་པས་ཕལ་ཆེར་
སྨག་དུ་འགུགས།། མ་ཁུགས་གོང་ལྟར་སྨན་དྱད་ཚ་བ་སྦྱང།། ཚ་ཐུར་དྱབ་ལ་འབྲས་ལྟར་རུལ་བཅོད་སྦྱར།། ཡང་ན་བྱི་ཤ་དཀར་མོ་གོ་དབྱེ་འཚལ་

Follow with hot water, sour grain-water, or rice water. Use the "Pomegranate Five" with boiled water.

<leaf-break/>

If Phlegm is dominant, treat it by choosing the specific food and medicine that counters it. When indigestion of the waste turns into other diseases, since it was originally produced by the cause of indigestion, use the "Pomegranate Five" mixed with salts and molasses. Delivering it with boiled water creates "stomach-fire." This clears the place of indigestion and allows the clear essence to remain in its own place. It will then be an ally in healing other resulting diseases. Trying to heal the result without treating the cause is like trying to extract poison by pouring in milk; it is like sour water. Since all internal diseases are produced by indigestion, the methods for treating indigestion are extremely important. If the cause itself is released, where can the result arise? Thus it was said. Then the sage Yid-las-skyes asked: "O Teacher, Sage Rig-pa'i Ye-shes, regarding the internal tumor diseases produced by the cause of indigestion: what are their causes, conditions, manner of arising, classifications, signs, methods of treatment, and how to cut off the remnants? May the King of Physicians explain it." The Teacher replied: "O great sage, listen. Regarding indigestion...

<leaf-break/>

...are the lungs, heart, liver, gallbladder, spleen, and kidneys. Also the bile-vessel, stomach, small intestine, "mound" <note>pubic area</note>, and "hollow" <note>lower abdomen</note>. Indigestion of waste from food and beans causes "intestine-masses" <term>go-long</term>. "Heart-tumors" <term>lhen-skran</term> <note>epigastric</note> and "stone-tumors" are in the stomach. "Wind-masses" <term>lhid-phran</term> reside in the stomach, large intestine, and the "hollow." Blood-tumors occur in the liver, spleen, stomach, and "hollow." Bile-tumors occur in the gallbladder and small intestine. Channel-tumors occur in the lungs, kidneys, liver, and "intestine-cords." Hair-tumors reside in the stomach, large intestine, small intestine, and "mound." Parasite-tumors occur in both the stomach and large intestine. Water-tumors are not fixed and can occur anywhere, though they are most common between the lungs, heart, liver, small intestine, and large intestine. "Sbag" tumors shift and have no fixed location. In brief, there are three types: external, internal, and intermediate tumors. External tumors are between the outer skin and the flesh of the vessels. Intermediate tumors are on the inner walls of the vessels or the sides of the solid organs. Disease-tumors reside in the very depths of all solid and hollow organs. As for the manner of arising: the accumulation of hard, fatty, or fermented foods, combined with old indigestion, creates mucus. This waste from indigestion turns into food tumors. Due to the condition of indigestion, Phlegm and mucus increase. When massed by Wind, it becomes what is called a "heart-tumor" <term>lhen-skran</term>. The clear essence from indigestion in the stomach...

There are six points for the great internal tumors: cause, condition, classification, location, manner of arising, signs, and methods of treatment. The causes are indigestion, Phlegm, blood, Bile, Wind, parasites, "water-serum" <term>chu-ser</term>, and hair. The conditions are past karma, demons, indigestion, spreading fever, agitation, wounds, and childbirth complications. The classifications are Phlegm-tumors, food-tumors, and stone-tumors; Wind-masses; blood, Bile, and channel tumors; water, parasite, hair, and 'sbag' tumors—eleven in total. The locations...

<leaf-break/>

...reside for a long time. When Phlegm and cold act as the cause and are massed by Wind, they repeatedly accumulate and ripen into hardness; this becomes what is called a "stone-tumor" from indigestion of the clear essence. When old indigestion causes bad blood to increase in the liver, droplets of blood form at the bottom of the liver. As they increase and mass, they become "liver blood-tumors." These may fall into the small intestine and mix with Bile. If they enter the spleen, they become "spleen tumors." If liver-blood falls into the stomach, it agitates the Phlegm. If it falls into the small intestine and mixes with Bile, it masses into a "small intestine bile-tumor." When indigestion causes Bile to drop and the Bile becomes a greasy mass, it is a "gallbladder tumor." When indigestion causes bad blood to increase and it moves to the liver-cord, lungs, kidneys, "intestine-cord," or the stomach channels, it masses in one place and becomes a "channel-tumor." བ་ལས༏ ༏བཀྱིལ་འཁོར་སྒོ་ཚོགས་སྤྲོ་བར་བྱ། །གཙོ་བོ་ཆེ་མཆོག་ཡབ་ཡུམ་ལ། །དྲེགས་པ་ཕྱོགས་སྐྱོང་འདུལ་བྱེད་བཅུ། །བཛྲ་ཧེ་རུ་ཡབ་ཡུམ་ལས། །ཀེ་རི་ཆེན་མོ་བརྒྱད་རྣམས་སྤྲོ། །འཇམ་དཔལ་གཤིན་རྗེ་ཡབ་
ཡུམ་ལས། །ཕྱོགས་སྐྱོང་བཅུ་གཉིས་འཁོར་དང་བཅས། །པདྨ་དབང་ཆེན་ཡབ་ཡུམ་ལས། །ཟིལ་གནོན་ཁྲོ་བོ་ཆེན་པོ་བརྒྱད། །རྡོ་རྗེ་གཞོན་ནུ་ཡབ་ཡུམ་ལས། །འཇིགས་པའི་ཁྲོ་བཅུ་ཁྲོ་མོར་བཅས། །བླ་མེད་ཧེ་རུ་ཡབ་

From the Accomplished Vajra-Holder,
The eight types of accomplished Knowledge-Holders.
On the outer gallery, the twenty-eight <term>Ishvaris</term> <gloss>goddesses</gloss>.
On the surrounding outer iron wall,
The Dakinis, Ging, Lanka,
Mothers, Sisters, Blazing Ones, Messengers,
And the hundreds of thousands of vast Dakinis
Who are the natural attendants of the Glorious One.
Thus, having clearly generated the essence,
Blessing the body, speech, and mind,
Empowering with the five wisdoms,
Invite them from their natural abode,
Offer, praise, and entrust them with activities.
Alternatively, the reality of the suchness of phenomena:
Leave it in the state of unconstructed self-radiance.
For whoever enters and has faith in this authentic path,
They will be joined to the level of spontaneous presence.
There is no doubt it can happen in a single lifetime.
Thus it was said.
From the Tantra of the Gathering of Sugatas, this is the ninth chapter: the perfectly condensed realization.
Next, the meaning of that very suchness
Will be explained in an extremely condensed way.
In a perfect-

Like a reflection in a mirror,
Appearing but indefinite, individually perceived.
Whoever meditates in that way,
Applies the ocean of activity to all.
Even a person who has committed the inexpiable sins,
If they practice, they will undoubtedly succeed.
Thus it was said.
From the Tantra of the Gathering of Sugatas, this is the tenth chapter: the extremely condensed realization.
This concludes the second section on the general realization of the wrathful deities.
Then, the Herukas of the four families
Requested: Ema! Universal Glory Heruka,
The means for the realization of the gathered qualities
Of all the Sugatas of the ten directions,
Please, Great Hero, explain it.
Having heard this request,
The Great Glorious Father commanded:
For those desiring the realization of the Great Supreme Qualities,
In a great isolated place of charnel grounds,
Having cleaned and polished the mandala,
Sprinkle it with the five nectars.
With the burning of great blood and great ash,
The skilled practitioner draws the dark blue syllable Hum.
Place that as the support for visualization.
When the three realms appear clearly,
The celestial palace of the great charnel ground
Has the five elements stacked,
And upon the Mount Meru of great skeletons,
The mandala of the terrifying charnel ground:
Four spokes, with porticos and galleries.
In the interior that is clear without outer or inner,
Possessing four gates with ornaments:
Upon the eight gods and eight nagas crossed,
And the eight chief animals,
From Hum arises the Great Supreme Heruka,
Together with the wrathful consort <term>Nam-zhel</term> <gloss>Sky-Face</gloss>.
Being the body of gathered qualities,
Generate them in the center of the wheel.
The Bhagavan Raksha Heruka,
With brownish-black, white, and red faces.
Holding a wheel, a lotus, and

Together with the summoning consort <term>Zhing-yum</term>,
The skilled practitioner generates them on the eastern spoke.
The Great Glorious Guhya Heruka,
With yellow-black, dark-blue, and red faces.
Holding a jewel, a skull-cup of blood, a battle-axe,
And a noose of intestines, the thousands of worlds
Having been seized, he performs union with the consort.
Generate them on the southern spoke.
The Bhagavan Visha Heruka,
With three heads: red-black, blue, and white.
Holding a lotus, a red bowl of the world,
A battle-axe, and likewise a <term>gshel</term> <gloss>ritual staff</gloss>,
Together with the wisdom consort:
With effort, generate them on the western spoke.
The Bhagavan Yaksha Heruka,
With green-black, white, and red faces.
With a double-vajra and a skull-cup of blood,
Holding a sword, a battle-axe, a noose,
And a plowshare, he joins with the consort.
Generate them on the northern spoke.
On the deity-platform of the outer rim:
The great wrathful subduers of the directions,
Holding a wheel and a trident,
The white-colored one is in the east.
Holding a battle-axe and a skull-staff,
The terrifying dark blue one is generated in the south.
The red one with a razor and noose
Is likewise in the western direction.
Holding a vajra-cross and a bell,
The green one is to be generated in the north.
Holding a fire-blaze and a club,
The red-colored one is in the southeast.
The great black one with a sword and noose
Is generated in the southwest.
Pinkish-red, holding a bowl and a whisk,
In the northwest.
A battle-axe and likewise a trident,
The blue one is generated in the northeast.
Pale blue, drawing a bow and arrow,
And smoke-colored, holding a hammer and noose,
Should be generated above and below;
Possessing the marks of their respective activities.

With dark-blue, white, and red faces.
Four legs, extended and drawn in, spread wide.
A vajra, a <term>khatvanga</term> <gloss>trident-staff</gloss>, and a small <term>de'u</term> drum in the right hands.

ནི་ཞུས་མ་ཐག །སངས་རྒྱས་ནམ་མཁའི་སྙིག་པོ་དེ། །ཨུད་པ་ལ་ཡིས་ཐུགས་དགྱེས་ཏེ། །ཞུས་པའི་ལན་དེ་བཀའ་སྩལ་པ། །གཞི་ལ་སྣང་མེད་ནམ་མཁའ་འདྲ། །མ་རིག་རྐྱེན་བྱས་གཟུང་འཛིན་གྱིས། །

"...that intention. For those who have not realized it, having meditated on the words, you should discuss it as much as appropriate so they may realize it through symbols."

When thus inspired, all the <term>Vidyadharas</term> <gloss>Knowledge-Holders</gloss> made a request from their hearts and replied with great gratitude: "The commands of the Lord of Gods <note>Indra</note> are a great kindness. May the faithful people of the human world of <term>Jambudvipa</term> clear away the darkness of ignorance! May they be blessed by the <term>Sugatas</term> <gloss>Those Gone to Bliss</gloss>!"

When this was said, the Great Knowledge-Holder, the Lord of Gods, was very pleased. The Lord of Gods then made this pledge: "If I am able to explain this great secret tantra of definitive meaning, without alteration or corruption, to a student who is a suitable vessel for the definitive truth, may I be blessed by the retinue of the Sugatas!"

Having made that pledge, listen further, Heart of the Assembly! Then the Son of the Gods thought: "Human beings lack clairvoyance and miraculous powers." Therefore, intending to explain it to the humans of Jambudvipa who were suitable vessels, he sought a support for his emanated birth. There was a woman of neither high nor low birth, <term>Yaksini Kunsö Jangchubma</term>. Intending to be born from her, he emanated as a golden-bodied swan with silver wings, iron claws, turquoise eyebrows, and vajra beak, with eyes made of precious gems. 

At dawn, as the sun rose, the bird came upon the sunbeams, touched its beak to the heart of <term>Jangchubma</term>, dissolved into her heart, and stayed for three days. A small boy was formed, firm as a stone...
stored.10:
"...since there is no inside or outside, how can there be [a distinction between] meditative equipoise and post-meditation?"

Having heard the meaning of that request, the Buddha Beholding a Hundred Thousand was pleased by the golden lotus and gave this answer: "In this very primordial wisdom awareness, there has never been meditative equipoise or post-meditation from the beginning. For a great meditator who lacks this definitive meaning, post-meditation arises in the mind of the five senses."

By that which was spoken, doubts about meditative equipoise and post-meditation were cut. Because the request was made, certainty was found. Therefore, primordial wisdom was manifested.

Then, that joyful Knowledge-Holder remembered his previous abode and went to the Cave of Precious Manifest Joy in the East of the Heaven of the Thirty-Three. By resting in meditative equipoise without result within, he went before <term>Sakra</term> <gloss>Indra</gloss>, Lord of the Gods, for the sake of all sentient beings, and inspired the Son of the Gods in this way:

"You are an emanation of <term>Shakyamuni</term>; you have no rival in the three worlds. All the teachings of the Buddha are perfect in your heart. For the suitable vessels of the Desire Realm of Jambudvipa, speak the Dharma that is realized just by being shown, in the form of well-composed verses."

When thus inspired, the Son of the Lord of Gods replied: "This great secret tantra of definitive meaning is clear from one's own mind, but since it does not fall into the domain of words, it is extremely difficult for me to explain."

When he had said that, the other understood the necessity and requested the meaning: "For the sake of the faithful ones of future generations, the authentic definitive meaning..."

<leaf-break/>

...the Lord [the boy] spoke these words as soon as he was born: "All phenomena are self-arising primordial wisdom. <term>Samsara</term> <gloss>cyclic existence</gloss> is ignorance from the very beginning. The essence is not produced by causes or conditions. One's own awareness is the <term>Dharmakaya</term> <gloss>Truth Body</gloss>."

Once such a proclamation was made, he was a wonder to this world. He was given the name <term>Garab Dorje</term> <gloss>Surpassing Joy Vajra</gloss>. Possessing the five sciences and qualities, he simultaneously knew the six clairvoyances. He was seen to be honored by all people. Invited by his qualities, he was requested to reside in the Abode of Bliss.

At that time, the emanation Garab [Dorje] remained continuously in the state of meditative absorption within. The <term>Yaksas</term> and demons were provoked, and for the sake of creating obstacles, the four Maras performed acts of intimidation and seduction. Knowing them to be the Maras of the gods, he did not lose mindfulness in the midst of the dizzying display. For the sake of compassion, he relaxed his meditative absorption. When they could not deceive him with either seduction or intimidation, the demons were discouraged and overwhelmed. To remove their anguish, they sought refuge:

"Great Compassionate One, look upon us! Through the karma of ignorance, we were born as <term>Rakshasas</term> <gloss>demons</gloss>. We ate the bodies and lives of sentient beings as food. We repent our evil karma in our minds. We shall protect your teachings. May we consume the bodies and lives of those who break their vows. I offer this, my life-essence; do not be small in your compassion!"

Having thus requested refuge, he offered his own life-essence to the Great Knowledge-Holder Garab Dorje, and promised to protect the teachings.

It will not be a teaching of the Shravaka <gloss>Hearer</gloss> vehicle. All sentient beings will be oriented toward self-arisen state <gloss>svayambhu</gloss> without being led astray. Then, for those world-experts who show the self-arisen Buddha-nature, the measure of their lifespan will be hundreds of millions of eons, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges. Ajita, rather than billions of Hearers in the world passing into Nirvana, if a single man or woman is made to delight in enlightenment, the former merit cannot even be compared to that in number or example. Therefore, O holy beings who have entered the path to enlightenment, delight in enlightenment. Ajita, it is not easy to find the arising of an All-Knowing Guide in this world. It is like the Udumbara flower, so says the Buddha of infinite intelligence. Therefore, whoever desires the supreme peace of enlightenment should rely on a Guide who is very subtle, a good companion, and skilled in the way of knowledge. Having heard such beneficial and pure speech from the mouth of the Tathagata, the entire assembly will be thrilled and exceedingly joyful. Billions of gods in the sky will wave their clothes. In their joy, they will shout: 'We prostrate to you, Buddha, the Powerful Lord!' You who are peaceful and whose heart is peace, make peaceful those beings who are agitated by the laughter of afflictions. You show the nectar and pacify the three poisons. Beings...
<leaf-break/>
and even if the head is cut off in every way, the perception of happiness will remain present. There will be no arising of any perception that is neither happy nor unhappy. Why is that? Because this Bodhisattva Mahasattva has for a long time, while practicing the conduct, made this aspiration: 'May those who have given me food obtain the happiness of pacification. May those who have given me drink, and those who have performed service for me, and those who have honored, respected, and made offerings to me, all obtain the happiness of pacification. Even those who abuse me, cause me unhappiness, strike me, hit me with weapons, and do everything up to taking my life—may they all obtain the happiness of enlightenment and awaken into unsurpassed, perfect, and complete Buddhahood.' Having made such aspirations and possessing those mental engagements, and through such karma and aspirations, they show, attend to, meditate on, and increase the perception of happiness that follows all sentient beings. From the ripening of that, they find happiness in all phenomena.

Then, after the gods of the Great Virtue realm <note>Subhakrtsna gods</note> spoke of this samadhi, they praised the Blessed One with these verses: 
"All these hosts of Great Virtue gods have reached the end of the Dharma. I take refuge by bowing my head to the Teacher whose senses are peaceful and who knows peace. Those wise ones who honor the Buddha, who know the meaning and have crossed the ocean of cyclic existence; I praise the Sage, the Guide of Men, the one skilled in the way, the Leader who leads the leaders. Here, there is no fixed 'Sage-Dharma' residing anywhere. Just as a magician knows his illusion, so you, O Sage, know it well. Just as a wise man understands that various limbs and echoes arise in the mountains, likewise, O Sugata, O Rishi, you view the world including its gods and men. Here, there is no sentient being, no life-force, no nourisher, no person. You, Supreme Man, have dismantled perceptions and established emptiness. O Best of Two-Legged Beings, foremost of sentient beings, you also meditate on immeasurable Compassion. This intention of the Victorious Buddha is difficult for all beings to realize. The Guide has spoken that meditating on the virtue of Compassion takes sentient beings as its object.

just as a man bitten by a venomous snake makes himself vomit phlegm in order to recover, the exhaustion of the phlegm of afflictions is liberation. That which is liberation is the Tathagata. Regarding "abandoning afflictions, abandoning afflictions," the exhaustion of afflictions which are like a venomous snake is liberation. That which is liberation is the Tathagata. Regarding "abandoning the aggregates, abandoning the aggregates," casting away all suffering so that bliss is predominant is liberation. That which is liberation is the Tathagata. Regarding "the exhaustion of desire, hatred, and ignorance," having exhausted the three and uprooted them is liberation. That which is liberation is the Tathagata. Regarding "abandoning all aggregates, abandoning all aggregates," it is the abandonment of all defects, for the sake of seeing correctly. That is liberation. That which is liberation is the Tathagata. Regarding "the purpose of abandoning all conditioned things," it is liberation, the accomplishment of all purity. That which is liberation is the Tathagata. Regarding "severance of the path," it is grasping selflessness in a manner that is continuous after meditating on selflessness,

<leaf-break/>

all attachment to craving, without exception, without remainder, without residue, the permanent and total pacification of all such desires is liberation; it is the cessation of all bonds. Such cessation is liberation. That which is liberation is the Tathagata. Regarding "Nirvana, Nirvana," it is like a herd of wild animals that has escaped from the hands of a hunter; terrified and frightened by death, they run with whatever means they have, and upon reaching the dwelling of a <term>rishi</term> <gloss>sage</gloss>, they become happy and find relief. Just as they find relief and happiness, just so, many sentient beings who do not know the end of Nirvana, having escaped the hands of all sounds of the types of afflictions and the conditioning of existence, are terrified and frightened by death. Running with whatever means they have, they go for refuge to the dwelling of the <term>Dharma-Rishi</term>, the Tathagata, the peerless refuge of the Muni's abode, and they find relief. Son of Noble Family, indeed it is so, for that is liberation. That is the Tathagata. He asked: If the realm of space is also unproduced and unarisen, should one say that liberation is also like that, and the Tathagata is also like that? He replied: It is not like that. Liberation is not like the realm of space. He asked: Then what is it like? He replied: Son of Noble Family, for example, when the <term>shang-shang-te'u</term> <gloss>a mythical bird with a human torso</gloss> or the <term>kalapingka</term> <gloss>cuckoo or Indian nightingale</gloss> utters a sound, is it said to be like the sound of a crow? He replied: Blessed One, it is not so. The sounds of other birds are not even suitable as examples for their sounds. The sound of a crow does not approach even a hundredth part of the sound of the <term>shang-shang-te'u</term> or the <term>kalapingka</term>. It does not approach even a thousandth part; it cannot bear the count, the fraction, the example, or the cause. Those birds are beyond example. Blessed One, the speech of the Tathagata is likewise beyond example by way of cause. He replied: Son of Noble Family, excellent, excellent! Son of Noble Family, it is right for you to explain it thus; it is excellent. Therefore, that which is liberation is the Tathagata. Other causes and examples for liberation do not exist in the world of gods, humans, and <term>asuras</term>.

ཡིན་ཏེ། །དེ་རྟེན་ཡུལ་དང་འབྲེལ་མེད་ཤེས། །དེ་ཚོར་བདེ་བ་འཇམ་དང་ཞིམ། །དགའ་བར་ཉམས་སུ་མྱོང་བའི་ཕྱིར། །ཡུལ་མེད་ཉམས་སུ་མྱོང་ཚད་ནི། །མན་ངག་
ལུང་ནི་ཆོས་སྐུར་ཤེས། །དེ་ཕྱིར་ཡེ་ཤེས་རང་ཤར་ཡིན། །དེ་ཡང་འདུས་པའི་སྙིང་པོ་ཉོན། །ཚོར་བ་མི་བདེ་སྡུག་བསྔལ་ཡང་། །ན་ཚ་མི་ཞི་རྩུབ་པ་དང་། །མི་དགའ་ལ་སོགས་ཅི་བྱུང་ཚེ། །ལུང་
ལྡན་རིན་ཆེན་རྐྱེན་གྱིས་ནི། །ཆོས་སྐུ་ཉམས་སུ་མྱོང་བའི་ཕྱིར།།ཡུལ་དང་གནས་སྐབས་མཐར་ཐུག་གི །འབྲེལ་པ་མེད་ཤེས་ཉམས་ཀྱི་ཚད། །དེ་ཡང་འདུས་པའི་སྙིངས་པོ་ཉོན། །ཡུལ་འདི་རིགས་
མེད་འཁྲུལ་པར་ཤེས། །འདུས་བྱས་ཡིན་ཕྱིར་ཆོས་སྐུ་མེད། །སྡུག་བསྔལ་ཚོར་བ་གང་བྱུང་ཡང་། །དེ་དུས་རྟགས་ཆད་མཐའ་མ་ལྟུང་། །བྱིང་རྒོད་གཉིས་ཀྱི་སྐྱོན་མ་གོས། །དེ་ཕྱིར་ཆོས་སྐུ་

to wish for the qualities of the form body to arise is called the "Katari-pa" of the non-Buddhists. How pitiful is the delusion of ignorance; it will become the great Unrelenting Hell.
From the Great Perfection, the Wheel of Primordial Wisdom, the Secret Tantra of the Heart, this is the tenth chapter, showing that the form body does not arise without being separated from the body.
Then, for the sake of the realization of the self-aware truth body, Vajrasatva requested the King of All-Knowing Dharma with these words of truthful meaning: "What is the pith instruction of self-arisen primordial wisdom that is not connected to the meaning of non-meditation? How does one perform the self-arisen conduct that does not fear ordinary conceptual thought? May the King of Equality please explain." Having heard the meaning of what was said, the All-Knowing Teacher spoke the certain meaning of self-arisen primordial wisdom that is never separated from non-meditation: "Regarding the logic of undeluded things, whatever sensations of bliss or suffering arise, through the condition of the jewel of the scriptures, one experiences that very thing as the truth body. Listen to this, Vajrasatva! Whatever forms of objects arise, through the awareness of undeluded things, it is the primordial wisdom grasped by the meaning; it is the perfect natural state of the intrinsic nature. Because that very thing, through the lamp of the scriptures, is without the darkness of ignorance, for the consciousness free from exaggeration and denigration, that is called the 'truth body.' Listen to this, Vajrasatva! For the faithful beginner, it is shown by pointing to the objects of things. The method is not to block appearances.

<leaf-break/>

Since that is so, know there is no connection between the support and the object. Because that sensation is experienced as pleasant, soft, and sweet, the measure of experiencing the objectless is knowing the scriptures of the pith instructions as the truth body. Therefore, it is self-arisen primordial wisdom. Listen to this, Essence of the Assembly! Even if the sensations are unpleasant and suffering, when sickness, non-pacified harshness, unhappiness, and so forth arise, because of the condition of the jewel of the scriptures, the truth body is experienced. Know that there is no connection between the object and the temporary or ultimate; that is the measure of experience. Listen to this, Essence of the Assembly! Know this object as a logicless delusion. Because it is conditioned, there is no truth body. Whatever sensations of suffering arise, at that time do not fall into the extremes of eternalism or nihilism. Do not be stained by the faults of dullness or agitation. Therefore, there is no need to meditate on the truth body. Listen to this, Vajrasatva! Whatever memories or thoughts of objects arise, because the truth body is experienced, know there is no connection between the six experiences. Rely on the nine modes of the method of realization. Regarding the insight that is able to withstand conditions, there is no need to divide it into the six types of withstanding conditions. Listen to this, Essence of the Assembly! In the view that does not grasp at extremes, awareness is clear as the relaxed truth body. Being grasped by the confidence of conviction is called the measure of possessing experience."
From the Great Perfection, the Wheel of Primordial Wisdom, the Secret Tantra of the Heart, this is the Chapter Teaching Self-Arisen Primordial Wisdom.

Through such certainty of decision, meditation and non-meditation are liberated in their own place. Since everything has become the truth body, because mind and objects are inseparable, the limit of space is not indicated, it is indeterminately perfect. Regarding the mind, appearances, and the phenomena of things, whatever memories of the mind appear, non-substantial awareness is clear as the truth body. It is free from the terminology of "meditation" and "non-meditation." Therefore, the primordial wisdom of mind and objects has dawned.
From the Great Perfection, the Wheel of Primordial Wisdom, the Secret Tantra of the Heart, this is the thirteenth chapter, Teaching the Conduct of the Self-Arising Primordial Wisdom of Mind and Objects.
Then, the supreme conduct of the <term>vratacharyā</term> <gloss>disciplined conduct</gloss> was spoken to the assembled host. For the sake of the realization of the view, coarse conduct must be cut through. There is a pith instruction for not being bound by it. Therefore, it is called self-liberated conceptual thought. Listen to this, Essence of the Assembly! A yogi who is shown by the certain scriptures may even use his mother and sister. What need is there to mention the women of others? Even if one tortures or kills sentient beings, or if one steals the wealth of the Sangha and the stupas, primordial wisdom dawns without the obscuration of conditions, just as the lord of hell is without downfall. In the supreme conduct of the <term>vratacharyā</term>, the sacred bonds of guarding are not contradicted; this dharma that accords with scripture and logic is necessary. Listen to this, Vajrasatva! Those who practice dharma in the present age, who desire a peaceful, gentle, and soft continuum, do not have the pith instructions.

With the middle finger, anointed with everything, for the three unchanging states in the three bodies, bless them with these mantras: <term>Om trimata bishodhaya ah hum</term>. 

Then, having completely purified the tooth-wood with this mantra, give it to the student. Having washed the teeth, with eyes covered and a pure intention, they should throw it upon it. Whichever direction it faces, based on the flower garland and the correspondence with the family, the accomplishment of that should be spoken. 

Then, for the blue protection-thread, after it has been purified by mantra, bind it on the right arm for men and the left for women. Examine the signs in the pillow and mat made of auspicious grass, which have been well placed. The wise one should examine whether there are good or bad omens, and whether one must avert them or not, just as they appear in other tantras. First perform the superior, middling, and inferior approach, and having performed the full approach at the end, the wise practitioner should then begin the perfect application.

<term>Om vajra samaya siddhi ah | Om sarva raksha sarva siddha ah hum |</term> 

Because of the necessity of the non-abiding nature, the taints of the conventional should be purified. Then, from the various riches, one should draw in full detail the mandala mentioned above. With excellent substances, one should perfectly offer with offerings.

<leaf-break/>

First, attachment to existence; in the middle, whatever remains; and at the end, whatever is destroyed: all mantras are spoken in detail. Being endowed with the five elements, from those and from all phenomena, the perfect state of total arising exists. The first meaning of the intense union with that, whatever is accomplished from this, and whatever the various rituals are, they are certainly without doubt. This is the fifth chapter, on the Inner and the Mantras, from the Tantra of the Adamantine Flame of the Blue-Clad Vajrapani. 

The blue-clad Vajrapani said this to the Victorious Protector: "For the sake of ripening sentient beings, I pray you, speak of the method of engagement." The All-Knowing Protector commanded: "First, the examination of the ground and so forth, as definitely explained above, all rituals should be certainly completed. རབ་རི་མོར་བཅས། །དབུས་ཀྱི་བྱང་ཆུབ་ཐིག་ལ་ལ། །གློ་གཏད་སྣང་མཛད་གནས་སུ་བྱིན། །དེ་ཡིས་སངས་རྒྱས་ཐམས་ཅད་བཀུག །ཡིད་བཞིན་ནོར་བུ་དང་འདྲར་འགྱུར། །འོག་
ནས་རང་གི་གནས་སུ་བསྡུ། །རྡོ་རྗེ་སེམས་པའི་གནས་དག་ཏུ། །བརྒྱད་དང་བཞི་ཡི་བདག་ཉིད་ཅན། །དང་པོ་ས་དང་འབྱུང་བ་ཡིས། །ངེས་པའི་རི་མོ་བསམ་པར་བྱ། །རང་གི་ས་
ནས་མཐའ་ཡས་བསྐུལ། །འདྲེས་པའི་བདེ་བའི་གནས་སུ་ཕྱིན། །ཐམས་ཅད་འདྲེས་པར་རང་གི་སར། །བདེ་དང་ལྡན་ནས་དེ་ཡིས་འགྲུབ། །སྤྲུལ་པའི་གནས་སུ་བཅུ་གསུམ་ལ། །
གཉིས་པ་གཉིས་དང་ཡང་དག་ལྡན། །ཡི་གེ་ཐིག་ལེ་བཅས་པོ་ཡིས། །འགྲོ་རྣམས་བདེ་བའི་གནས་སུ་སྤྲོས། །སླར་འདུས་དེ་རུ་དངོས་གྲུབ་འགྱུར། །ཡང་ན་རྟག་ཆད་བྲལ་བ་ཡི། །

Also perfectly generate oneself in that very essence by residing in the form of that very thing. Having perfectly wrapped the lotus itself and the clothing and so forth with blue, one should sprinkle and enter with scented water using the mantra of the Swirling Nectar. From remaining definitely in front, according to whatever wealth of that size is available, make the fees be taken as pure. 

I shall hold the palms together and speak in detail of the generation of the mind and so forth. From the certainty of the various appearances, the family should be subsequently held. Throw the garland of blue flowers while speaking the mantra. Having thus shown the assembly of deities, the empowerment given to the student by the master himself with the water of the vase is the vase empowerment; it is considered the purification of the coarse. 

Then, through the performing of the gesture, with the mind of awakening unimpaired, whichever of self or others is suitable, after perfectly manifesting bliss and having perfectly joined it with intention, one should give into their mouth through the gesture of method and wisdom. Those are the secret empowerments, and after that, one is purified.

མཚམས་སྦྱོར་དུ་མ་ཡོད་པས་སོ། །དེ་ན་འདི་དག་འགོག་པ་མེད་པའི་རང་བཞིན་གྱི་མཚམས་སྦྱོར་ལྟ་བུ་ནི་གཉིས་ཀ་ཡིན་ཡང་གཞན་ལ་མ་ངེས་སོ། །མཆོད་བརྗོད་བྱས་པས་གཞན་དག་དང་། །བསྐྱེད་ཅེས་བསྟན་ན། གཞན་དག་ནི་གང་། མཆོད་བརྗོད་ལས་ནི་ཇི་ལྟར་དང་ཞེ་ན། འདི་ལ་གཉིས་
དབང་བརྟུལ་དང་། དབང་རྣོན་གྱི་ངང་ཚུལ་ལོ། །དང་པོ་ནི། གང་ཟག་གཙོ་བོར་བྱས་ནས་འཇུག་པའམ་ཚིག་ཙམ་ལས་ཡིད་ཆེས་སྐྱེ་བའི་དད་པའི་རྗེས་སུ་འབྲང་བ་རྣམས་ནི་དང་བ་སྐྱེའོ། །ངོ་བོ་ནི་རབ་ཏུ་སྟེ་ཆེན་པོའོ། །རེ་ཞིག་ནི་བཤད་པའི་རིམ་པའམ་འདི་དབང་རྣོན་ལས་དང་པོ་སྐྱེ་མྱུར་བའོ། །
ཡུལ་ནི་ཡུམ་འདི་ལའོ། །ཚུལ་ནི་ཡུམ་སྔར་བཤད་པའི་ཡོན་ཏན་དང་ལྡན་པར་བསྟན་པ་ནི་ཡོན་ཏན་དེ་ལྟ་བུ་དང་ལྡན་པ་ཡིན་ནམ་མིན་སྙམ་པའི་ཐེ་ཚོམ་མེད་པར་ཏེ་བརྟགས་དཔྱད་མ་བྱས་པར་ཚིག་ཐོས་མ་ཐག་ཏུ་སྐྱེ་བས་ན་མྱུར་དུའོ། །རྒྱུ་ནི་ཉན་ཐོས་ཞེས་སོགས་ཚིགས་བཅད་འདིས་ནི་ཡུམ་
འདིས་སྲས་བཞིའི་བཞེད་པ་བསྐྲུན་པའི་ཆེ་བའི་བདག་ཉིད་ཀྱི་ཡོན་ཏན་གསུམ་པོ་ཕྱི་རོལ་པ་དང་ཉན་རང་དང་བྱང་སེམས་ལས་ཕུལ་དུ་བྱུང་བ་དང་ལྡན་པར་བརྗོད་དེ་བརྗོད་པ་དེ་ཐོས་པ་ལ་བརྟེན་ནས་སོ། །གཉིས་པ་ནི་དབང་བརྟུལ་ཁོ་ནར་མ་ཟད་ཆོས་གཙོ་བོར་བྱས་ནས་འཇུག་བའམ། དོན་
ལ་བརྟགས་དཔྱད་བྱས་ནས་འཇུག་པའི་ཆོས་ཀྱི་རྗེས་སུ་འབྲང་བ་རྣམས་ཀྱང་དང་བ་བསྐྱེད་པར་བྱེད་པར་བྱང་བ་ཉིད་དོ་ཞེས་རྣམ་པར་སྦྱར་རོ། །དང་བའི་ངོ་བོ་ནི་རབ་ཏུ་སྟེ་མི་འཕྲོགས་པའོ། །གང་ལ་ན་ཡུམ་དེ་ལའོ། །འདིར་དེ་དང་གོང་དུ་འདི་ཞེས་པ་ནི་མཆོད་བརྗོད་ལ་ཉེ་རིང་གི་ཡིན་ནོ། །
རྒྱན་སྔར་ལྟར་རོ། །ཚུལ་ནི་འོ་ན་ཡུམ་གྱི་སྲས་བཞི་བསྐྲུན་པར་མཛད་དོ་ཞེས་བསྟན་པ་ཙམ་གྱི་མདོ་ལ་ཡིན་ནམ་ཞི་མ་མ་ཡིན་ཏེ། འདི་ལྟར་སྤྱིར་དབང་བརྟུལ་གྱི་འཇུག་ལྡོག་གི་རྒྱུ་ཚིག་ཙམ་ཡིན་ཡང་། དབང་སྣོན་ནི་རིགས་པས་གནོད་པ་ཡོད་མེད་བརྟགས་པ་ན་གནོད་པ་མེད་པ་དང་ཡོད་པར་

གྱིས་མི་ཆག་ག་སྒྲུབ་བྱེད་བཟུང་བ་ཡང་དགོས་མེད། འདིར་ནི་དབང་རྟུལ་དང་བ་ན་གནོད་མི་གནོད་མ་མཐོང་བར་ཡུམ་གྱིས་སྲས་བསྐྲུན་པར་བསྟན་པ་བདེན་པར་གཟུང་བ་ལྟ་བུ་མིན་གྱི ། གནོད་པ་ཡོད་མེད་བརྟགས་པ་ནི་མི་གནོད་པར་མཐོང་ནས་སྲས་རྣམས་བསྐྲུན་པར་བཟུང་སྟེ ། ཞེས་བཤད་པ་དགོས
པས་གཞུང་དེ་གཉིས་སོ་སོར་གནོད་པ་མི་འཐད་དོ ། །གཞུང་གཉིས་པ་ནི་བསྒྲུབ་བྱ་དུ་སྣང་བའི་ཕྱིར་སྒྲུབ་བྱེད་གཟུང་བ་རུ་མི་འཐད་དོ ། །འོ་ན་སྒྲུབ་བྱེད་གཟུང་བ་གང་ཞེ་ན ། སྔར་བཤད་པ་ལྟར་མཆོད་བརྗོད་ཀྱིས་བསྟར་ཚོང་དང་དབུ་མའི་རིགས་པ་རྣམས་འགལ་བ་ལྟར་སྣང་ནས་མི་དང་བ་ལ་བརྟགས

ཟིན་ཅིང་ ། གཞི་ལམ་རྣམ་གསུམ་སྐྱེ་མེད་ནི་མ་ཟིན་པའི་ཕྱིར་རོ ། །ཚིག་གསལ་དུ་ཁྱད་གཞི་ནི་ཤེར་ཕྱིན་ནོ ། །ཁྱད་པར་ནི་མཁྱེན་གསུམ་མོ ། །གསུམ་དུ་བསྟན་པ་ཡང་ཀུན་རྫོབ་ཏུ་ཡང་དབྱེར་མེད་དོ་སྙམ་པ་དགག་པ་དང་ ། སྲས་གསུམ་ཆེར་སྐྱེ་བར་བསྟན་པའི་ཕྱིར་ཏེ ། སངས་རྒྱས་རྣམས་དཔར་སངས་རྒྱས། །

it is not broken by that, so identifying a proof is unnecessary. Here, it is not like the dull-witted whose faith consists of taking the Mother's production of sons as true without seeing whether it is damaged or not. Instead, one must explain that "having investigated whether there is damage or not and seeing no damage, one grasps that she produces the sons." Thus, it is unreasonable for those two texts to be separate. The second text is unreasonable as an identification of a proof because the object to be proven appears as two. 

What then is the identification of the proof? As explained before, the descriptions in the opening praise and the reasonings of the Middle Way <note>Madhyamaka</note> appear to be contradictory. At the time of investigation, those who were not faithful see that the two are not contradictory; since faith arises merely from that, what is the point of identifying other proofs? The second point is also unreasonable because the investigation into whether there is damage by reasoning applies to the literal extent of the opening praise. In that literal extent, the Mother producing the sons is present, but the birthlessness of the three of base and path is not.

In the *Clear Words*, the "basis of the quality" is the Perfection of Wisdom. The "quality" is the three kinds of omniscience. Showing her as three is to refute the thought that they are indistinguishable even conventionally, and to show how the sons are greatly produced. For it is praised: "The path of liberation for the Buddhas and that which is definitely relied upon by the Hearers is you alone; there is no other." 

One might think that this would mean there is nothing in this Mother that is superior to the individual realizations of the vehicles, and nothing in this Sutra that teaches her that is superior to other Sutras. This is because the part that produces the Hearers and Solitary Realizers would be merely the realization of the selflessness of persons, and the part that produces Bodhisattvas and Buddhas would be the realization of the two selflessnesses. Since those are taught respectively in the *Mindfulness* <note>original: Smra bar bzhag</note> and the *Array of Stalks* <note>original: Sdong po bkod pa</note> Sutras, to clear that away, it says "endowed with the three-fold manner."

<leaf-break/>

it follows that there would be none. This is because there is no liberation apart from the Mother, and yet the Mother would not be the path for these. One cannot accept that. These two reasons are drawn from the scripture of praise as the evidence and are accepted by the two root tenets. If one holds the Knowledge of Bases and Knowledge of Paths to be the Mother of the Buddha alone, then the two persons shown as the Hearer and the Bodhisattva would also become metaphorical. Therefore, such an explanation, which collects many contradictions, is a mockery of both Maitreya and the Master <note>Haribhadra</note>. Those who follow this have also failed to investigate well. 

Therefore, the meaning of "manner"—which was the basis of confusion—is as intended in the "establishment of the three manners," which the *Hundred Thousand* <note>original: Bum pa</note> accepts as the "three-fold manner of the vehicles," or it is explained as the "three-fold manner of dividing into three knowledges." 

If someone says, "Even the Master considers the paths of the vehicles to be metaphorical Perfection of Wisdom, so there is no inconsistency, because the Perfection of Wisdom and the Mother have the same meaning," this is most unreasonable. The meaning of "Mother" is merely the fulfillment of the unique aims of the four sons. How could the Master say that does not exist for Hearers and Bodhisattvas? Furthermore, since they would lack the actual Mother, the sons would also become metaphorical. By saying that the division into three knowledges is not a division into separate natures, and that although they appear as many they are only one essence, he refutes the view of the *Clear Words* that says the Mother of the Bodhisattva is actual but that of the Hearer is not—for he holds them to be one with the actual Omniscience and thus the Mother of the Buddha alone. Enough of this elaboration.

The second part: when it is said "for the purpose of causing them to enter by way of the meaning," if one asks "how do they enter?", they "act with respect." Toward what? Qualities of that Mother such as "leading to the profound peace."
